Scope: master index and cross-reference of the x3650m3-kb knowledge base (Wave 3, docs/KB_PLAN.md). This document holds no facts of its own: every value below is copied from the detail document it links to, and the linked document (with its sources and truth levels, docs/AGENT.md) is authoritative. When two documents disagree, the disagreement is listed in section 4, not resolved here. Compiled offline on 2026-10-20 from the repository state at commit 758cd44 and refreshed the same day against the working tree after commit dcb80e1, including the integration of the 2026-10-20 SMART, verbose SDR / M1015 slot detail and IMM CLI settings captures; no command was run against the server, the IMM or the internet. The owner's server is an IBM System x3650 M3, type-model 7945KEG, serial [redacted-id] (HW 2), and it is also the Proxmox VE 8.4.0 host [lab-ip] (hostname [lab-host], pve-manager 8.4.21, kernel 6.8.12-43-pve) that runs the agent container (TOOLS 2; ASSUMPTIONS A-007). It has one Intel Xeon E5606 2.13 GHz (4 cores, Westmere-EP, model 44 stepping 2) in socket 1 with socket 2 unpopulated (HW 2, SYSARCH 3), running microcode 0x14 (OPT 1). Memory is one 8 GB RDIMM in slot DIMM03 (SK Hynix HMT31GR7BFR4A-H9, 2 ranks, x4) at 1067 MT/s, 17 of 18 slots empty (MEM 1, MEM 9). Storage is a ServeRAID M1015 (LSI SAS2008, firmware package 20.10.1-0052, no Advanced Feature Key, no BBU) with VD 0 (RAID0, 231.898 GB, Toshiba MK2546GSX at 64:0, Proxmox boot disk /dev/sda) and, since 2026-10-20, VD 1 "hitachi_data" (RAID0, 110.827 GB, Hitachi HTS542512K9SA00 at 64:1, /dev/sdb, ext4, Proxmox storage hitachi-data, target of the weekly vzdump job); neither VD is redundant; a second SAS2008 HBA (IBM 6Gb SAS HBA 9212-4i4e) has no devices attached (STOR 1). SMART on 2026-10-20: Toshiba 14179 power-on hours, no logged error; Hitachi 1311 power-on hours, 0 reallocated/pending, 140 logged ATA UNC read errors at 1189 h; no self-test has ever run on either drive, long self-tests are queued (STOR 6.1). The IMM sees one power supply, named "Power Supply 2" in IPMI FRU/SDR but "Power Supply 1" in its own VPD (FRU 39Y7229, CANDIDATE 460 W AC) (HW 10). The IMM is the first-generation Integrated Management Module (S-002, S-004, S-001 refer to "IMM"; IMM2 is the M4 generation and not used here). Version in the measured unit: IMM build YUOOC7E (2011-09-30), UEFI D6E154A (2011-09-23) per IMM CLI vpd (C-IMMCLI); BMC firmware revision 1.30, IPMI 2.0, manufacturer ID 2 (IBM), product ID 0x00dc, aux revision bytes 0x00 0x00 0x1b 0x41 (C-IPMI mc info). SMBIOS OEM string "$SI Integrated Management Module 1.30 -[YUOOC7E-1.30]-" (C-OS dmidecode type 11). SMBIOS BIOS version "-[D6E154AUS-1.13]-", release 09/23/2011 (C-OS dmidecode). MEASURED. The firmware-level reasons for these numbers are covered in X3650M3_FIRMWARE_HISTORY.md. Attachment paths seen from the host (all MEASURED): Path Evidence Detail LPC / KCS (in-band IPMI) SMBIOS type 38: KCS, spec 2.0, base 0x0ca2 (I/O), "I2C slave address 0x10", NV storage not present (C-OS dmidecode); PNP device IPI0001 I/O 0xca2 and 0xca3 (C-PNP); ipmi_si kernel log "kcs state machine at i/o address 0xca2, slave address 0x20, irq 0", BMC found man_id 0x2, prod_id 0xdc, dev_id 0x20 (C-OS dmesg) Standard KCS layout: data register at the base 0xca2 and status/command register at 0xca3 (CANDIDATE, from the IPMI KCS convention and the two PNP I/O ranges). No interrupt (irq 0): polled. The SMBIOS slave address 0x10 and the kernel's 0x20 are the same address in 7-bit and 8-bit notation (CANDIDATE: 0x20 >> 1 == 0x10). /dev/ipmi0 is the in-band interface (docs/AGENT.md). Host USB controllers: five UHCI (1.1) plus two EHCI (2.0), all ICH10 (Section 6). Seven root hubs: usb1/usb2 (EHCI, 2.0), usb3-usb7 (UHCI, 1.1) (C-USB, C-RES). MEASURED. Sysfs mapping: usb1=1a.7, usb2=1d.7, usb3=1a.0, usb4=1a.1, usb5=1d.0, usb6=1d.1, usb7=1d.2 (C-RES). MEASURED. External ports: two on the front, two on the rear, plus an internal port for an embedded hypervisor key (S-001 p.7 Table 1; S-002 p.7 Table 1 says four USB ports "two on front, two on rear" plus one or more dedicated internal USB ports on the SAS riser-card, and hypervisor support through an optional USB flash device on the SAS riser-card "not available on simple-swap models"; hypervisor key: S-002 "Removing a USB hypervisor memory key", p.148). DOCUMENTED. SMBIOS lists USB 1-4 as port connectors (C-OS dmidecode type 8). MEASURED. The only enumerated non-hub device is the IMM LAN-over-USB device (04b3:4010) at bus 5 port 2 (C-USB). No front/rear/internal USB devices were attached at capture time, so which root hub serves which physical port is UNKNOWN (needs the owner to plug a device into each port while lsusb -t runs). No USB hypervisor key is present: lsusb on 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-21 lists only root hubs and the IMM device (MEASURED by absence, captures/2026-10-19_hw_lsusb_v.txt, captures/2026-10-21_host_cpu_power_thermal_readonly.txt). The RMRR reserved region used by all seven USB controllers (Section 4) is consistent with USB-based IMM remote media (CANDIDATE).

entries.h: 6. Operator information panel and light path diagnostics
6.1 Operator information panel (front, S-002 p.16-17; S-004 p.12)
entries.x: Control or LED Behaviour Power-control button and power-on LED Off: no AC or failed supply/LED. Flashing rapidly (4 per second): server off and not ready, button disabled, lasts about 20-40 s. Flashing slowly (1 per second): off and ready to be turned on. Lit: server on. Fading on and off: reduced-power state (wake by button or IMM web). Ethernet icon LED Lights the Ethernet icon Ethernet activity LEDs Traffic on the corresponding Ethernet port Information LED Noncritical event occurred; an LED on the light path panel is also lit System-error LED System error occurred; a light path panel LED is also lit Release latch Slide left to pull out the panel and expose the light path diagnostics panel Locator button and LED (blue) Identifies the server; the IMM CLI command identify controls the same LED remotely The panel assembly is a Tier 1 CRU (part 44E4372, cable 46C4139 FRU). Power-button readiness delay: conflict C-3.

The panel sits on top of the operator information panel; slide the blue release latch left and pull it forward to view it. Do not run the server for an extended time with the panel pulled out. It has the Remind button, NMI button (only on IBM support's instruction), Reset button (lower-right corner, recessed: resets and runs POST) and a checkpoint code display (shows POST/boot-block checkpoint codes for IBM service, not error codes). Sources: S-002 pp.16-17; S-004 pp.12-13; IC:c_light_path_diagnostic_panel, IC:t_light_path_diagnostics. DOCUMENTED. Panel layout (S-004 Fig 4, p.13), LED labels in three rows: Row LEDs (left to right) 1 OVERSPEC, LOG, LINK, PS, PCI, SP 2 FAN, TEMP, MEM, NMI (below LOG, LINK, PS, PCI) 3 CNFG, CPU, VRM, DASD, RAID, BRD To the right: REMIND button, NMI button (small, recessed), two-digit checkpoint code display, RESET button (lower right). DOCUMENTED (S-004 Fig 4). Remind: puts the system-error LED into Remind mode (flash once every 2 s) until the problem is corrected, the server restarts or a new problem occurs. Controlled by the IMM (IC:c_remind_button).

A server with an Intel Xeon X5600 series CPU runs at up to 1333 MHz with two DIMMs per channel when: two 1.5 V single/dual-rank RDIMMs per channel and Setup "Memory speed" = Max performance, or two 1.35 V single/dual-rank RDIMMs per channel, "Memory speed" = Max performance and "LV-DIMM power" = Enhance performance; the 1.35 V RDIMMs then run at 1.5 V. Source: S-002 and S-004 ("Installing a memory module"). Level: DOCUMENTED. The text says "X5600 series"; whether the E5606 qualifies is not stated (it is a Xeon 5600 series part but is limited by its own memory-speed rating, see 5.3). The UEFI 1.22 setup XML additionally has uEFI.Plt2DPC1333Capable ("2DPC1333 Capable", default Disable) and uEFI.Enable2DPCOverclock ("2DPC Overclocking", default Disable) (docs/X3650M3_UEFI.md Appendix A, EXTRACTED); their relation to the S-002 conditions is not documented (CANDIDATE: firmware side of the same rule).

TIPS0805 states "up to 1333 MHz memory speed" for the 5600 family and lists per-model memory speeds: model 7945-22x (1x Xeon E5606 2.13 GHz, 4C, 8 MB) = 1066 MHz; E5645/X5650/L5640 models = 1333 MHz. Source: S-001 Table 1 (standard specifications) and Table 2 (standard models). Level: DOCUMENTED. S-001 "Memory options" also states that the maximum memory speed is limited by the processor's supported speed and by the DIMM count/type, whichever is lower. The owner's CPU is an E5606 (captures/2026-10-19_hw_cpuinfo.txt, model 44, stepping 2). Level: MEASURED. The maximum DDR3 speed of this CPU is therefore 1066 MHz (DOCUMENTED via the 7945-22x row; the DIMM in the machine runs at the same value, MEASURED, section 9). Only the 7945-22x row of S-001 Table 2 names the E5606; the E5606 is not in the S-001 processor option table. Other 4C rows with "1066 MHz" (E5603, E5607, E5620) use other CPUs. Intel specification for the E5606 (intel.com ark, SKU 52583, "Intel Xeon Processor E5606 (8M Cache, 2.13 GHz, 4.80 GT/s Intel QPI)" specifications page, research 2026-10-21): memory types DDR3 800/1066, 3 channels, max 288 GB, max bandwidth 25.6 GB/s, ECC supported, QPI 4.8 GT/s with 2 links, TDP 80 W, no Turbo, no Hyper-Threading. RAS per the Xeon 5600 datasheet vol 2 (Table 3-1, Sec 3.4): x4 SDDC in independent channel mode, x8 SDDC in lockstep (Ch0+Ch1), mirroring Ch0+Ch1 with Ch2 empty, sparing with Ch2 as the spare (5600 only). Server supports 1.5 V and 1.35 V (low-voltage, "PC3L") DDR3 DIMMs. Mixing 1.5 V and 1.35 V DIMMs is supported on Xeon 5600 systems; all DIMMs then run at 1.5 V. Xeon 5500 systems do not support 1.35 V DIMMs. Source: S-001 "Memory options". Level: DOCUMENTED. 1.35 V DIMMs "consume 20 percent less energy". Source: S-001 (features list). Level: DOCUMENTED (vendor claim). Correction 2026-10-21: ipmitool prints 1.5 V Nominal Op: Yes, 1.35 V Nominal Op: No, 1.2X V Nominal Op: Yes (captures/2026-10-19_ipmi_inband.txt, FRU DIMM 3, MEASURED). ipmitool lib/dimm_spd.c prints "No" when the bit is set for all three bits of SPD byte 6 ((spd_data[6]&2) != 0 ? "No":"Yes", https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ipmitool/ipmitool/master/lib/dimm_spd.c), but JEDEC Std 21-C 4.1.2.11 (DDR3 SPD, byte 6 "Module Nominal Voltage, VDD") defines bit 0 = 1 as "NOT 1.5 V operable" and bits 1 / 2 = 1 as "1.35 V operable" / "1.25 V operable". "1.2X V" is the 1.25 V bit. The printed lines therefore mean byte 6 = 0x02: 1.5 V operable, 1.35 V operable, not 1.25 V operable (CANDIDATE, derived from the ipmitool source and JEDEC; the raw byte was not read). The earlier statement "1.5 V only" rested on the inverted ipmitool text and is withdrawn; the module runs at 1.5 V here in any case (single DIMM, LV-DIMM Power "Low Power" acts only with two 1.35 V DIMMs on a channel and a 1333 MHz CPU, UEFI help text, docs/X3650M3_UEFI.md 12.7). UEFI controls: Memory speed, LV-DIMM power (see 8).

entries.h: 6. Population rules and order per mode
entries.x: Modes named in the vendor documents: normal (independent channels), memory mirroring, online-spare (sparing). No document in the local source set mentions a "lockstep" mode for this server, and the UEFI 1.22 setup XML offers only Independent (default), Mirroring and Sparing for uEFI.MemoryChannelMode (docs/X3650M3_UEFI.md section 7 and Appendix A, EXTRACTED). Lockstep is therefore not a selectable mode in that firmware release.

"In non-mirroring mode, all three channels on the memory interface for each microprocessor can be populated in any order and have no matching requirements." For performance use the sequence in section 3.2. Source: S-002 Table 10 text; infocenter c_dimm_installation_sequence_option. Level: DOCUMENTED. Minimum configuration: S-002 says the server ships with at least one 2 GB DIMM in slot 3; S-004 / infocenter r_memory_problems say "one 1 GB DIMM in slot 3". See conflict C-2. Each installed CPU needs at least one DIMM. Level: DOCUMENTED (S-002).

Pair CPUs installed Connectors 1 1 3 + 6 2 1 2 + 5 3 1 1 + 4 4 2 12 + 15 5 2 11 + 14 6 2 10 + 13 Pairs are on channel 0 and channel 1 of the same CPU, same connector position (3-6, 2-5, 1-4). Channel 2 connectors 7, 8, 9, 16, 17, 18 are unused in mirroring mode. The two DIMMs of a pair must be identical in size, type, rank (single/dual/quad) and organization; speed may differ (the channels run at the slowest). Addressable memory = half of installed (example: 64 GB installed => 32 GB). Enable: Setup utility -> System Settings -> Memory -> Memory Channel Mode -> Mirroring. Memory for CPU2 may be added as soon as CPU2 is installed. S-001 "Memory options": with mirroring, DIMMs are installed in pairs with a minimum of one pair per CPU. Maximum mirrored capacity with 1 CPU: 6 DIMMs; with 16 GB dual-rank RDIMMs 96 GB installed, 48 GB usable; with two CPUs 192 GB installed, 96 GB usable (derived arithmetic from the rules above). Level: DOCUMENTED rules, derived numbers. Source: S-002 "Memory mirroring" (Tables 11, 12), infocenter c_memory_mirroring_option. Level: DOCUMENTED. The explanatory prose next to Figures 122 and 123 in the same section contradicts Tables 11/12; the figure labels themselves (text layer) agree with the tables (conflict C-4).

CPU Connector sets (cumulative) CPU1 3, 6, 9 -> then add 2, 5, 8 -> then add 1, 4, 7 CPU2 12, 15, 18 -> then 11, 14, 17 -> then 10, 13, 16 Supported only on models with a Xeon 5600 series CPU (S-002; S-001 repeats "only supported for Intel Xeon 5600 series"). DIMMs are installed three per CPU at a time (one per channel): first DIMM channel 0, second channel 1, spare DIMM channel 2. DIMMs in a set must be identical in size, type, rank, organization; speed may differ. Usable memory = 2/3 of installed (example: 72 GB installed => 48 GB usable). Sparing and mirroring are alternatives: "You can enable either online-spare memory or memory mirroring". Triggering threshold for sparing: Setup question "Spare Error Threshold" (Memory form, docs/X3650M3_UEFI.md section 5, EXTRACTED) / ASU name uEFI.SpareErrorThreshold (S-026); sub-setting of MemoryChannelMode, numeric 0..15, default 15, protected (docs/X3650M3_UEFI.md Appendix A.2, EXTRACTED). Source: S-002 "Online-spare memory" (Table 13); infocenter c_online_spare_memory_option; S-001 "Memory options". Level: DOCUMENTED.

Today only connector 3 is populated, one CPU: independent mode, one channel used (channel 0). Mirroring needs 2 identical DIMMs (3+6); sparing needs 3 identical DIMMs (3+6+9). System Settings -> Memory: view or change memory settings; Memory Channel Mode -> Mirroring enables mirroring (S-002 "Setup utility menu choices", S-004 same text, infocenter c_setup_uility_menu_choices). "Memory speed" (value "Max performance") and "LV-DIMM power" (value "Enhance performance") determine the 2-DPC speed rule (S-002/S-004, section 5.2). The Setup utility shows installed memory and, after a change of the memory configuration, the system reports a configuration change at the next restart (S-002). DIMMs can be enabled or disabled in Setup after POST/SMI disabled them (infocenter r_memory_problems). Menu item names for that are not given in the vendor documents. CANDIDATE: the Memory form's "Planar DIMM Details" form and the setting uEFI.MemorySlotDisableControl ("Memory Slot DIMM Enable") found in the UEFI 1.22 image (docs/X3650M3_UEFI.md sections 5 and Appendix A, EXTRACTED); the link to the r_memory_problems wording is an inference.

entries.h: 5. Drive bays, backplanes, SAS riser and cabling

entries.x: S-001 "Internal storage": four 2.5" SATA simple-swap bays (CTO only), four hot-swap, eight hot-swap, sixteen hot-swap, or eight hot-swap plus internal tape. S-002 (Table 1 "Features and specifications", depending on the model): eight 2.5" SAS hot-swap bays with the option to add eight more, or four 2.5" simple-swap SATA/SSD bays; "What your server offers": up to eight or sixteen 2.5" hot-swap drives depending on model and options. Bay IDs 0-7 (and 0-15 with the 8-pack option) are printed on the front above each bay (S-002 figures 1-3). All bays are 2.5" SFF: there are no 3.5" hard-disk bays in this machine type; the 3.5" items in S-002 are tape/RDX bezels, and 3.5" drives appear in S-001 only as external EXP enclosure options. Standard models: A2x ships with four bays, all other models with eight (S-001 "Internal drive configurations").

entries.h: 9.2 Expected thermal and power effect on this server (CANDIDATE unless noted)
entries.x: Turbo Mode has no effect: the E5606 has no Turbo Boost (S-001 p.12, DOCUMENTED; no "ida" flag, MEASURED). Processor Performance States: with P-states the CPU can drop from 2128 MHz (80.0 W declared) to 1197 MHz (46.3 W declared); the declared difference is 80.000 - 46.255 = 33.745 W at full load (C-ACPI arithmetic). At light load most savings come from idle states rather than P-states; the kernel already requests C6 for most idle time (section 5.3), but the wattage saved is UNKNOWN (needs before/after Avg Power with a setting change, excluded by D-006). Performance mode disables P-states and C1E, so the CPU stays at 2128 MHz and idles at a higher power; the IMM has a "fan control enhancement for performance mode" (IMM 1.14, DOCUMENTED), so higher fan speed is expected in Performance mode (CANDIDATE, mechanism UNKNOWN). Memory and QPI "Minimal Power" lower memory and link clocks; with one DIMM the absolute saving is small (CANDIDATE; no wattage source). The DIMM already runs at 1067 MT/s (docs/X3650M3_MEMORY.md). Acoustic mode is described as lowest power and lower acoustic level (EXTRACTED help text); how the IMM fan curve changes in that mode is not documented (UNKNOWN). C-states: the installed 1.13 has "Power C-States" (uEFI.ProcessorCcxEnable) = Disable and the package C-state limit = ACPI C3 (MEASURED; 1.22 defaults Disable / ACPI C2); the FADT advertises no ACPI C2/C3 (section 5.3), but intel_idle requests C6 anyway (section 5.3). The effect of enabling ACPI C-states on

Memory form question "Thermal Mode" (qid 0x0013, varstore offset 0x0665): options "Normal" = 0 (default) and "Performance" = 1; help: "Select this to set your Thermal Mode Options. Changes won't take effect until the next boot." (UEFI-HII, 1.22). The 1.14 and 1.22 setup XML contain a Thermal_Mode setting (Normal = 0 default, Performance = 1, Acoustic = 2) with per-mode protected sub-settings: Hysteresis (0 / 1.5 default / 3 / 6 deg C), Upper Boundary Alarm Trip Temperature (default 75 deg C, 0-128), Critical Alarm Trip Temperature (default 80 deg C), memory controller throttle duty cycle (LSB default 3FFF), memory refresh rate (Single default / Double). The whole block is inside an XML comment, so ASU most likely does not expose it (CANDIDATE, reason: commented out in the XML ASU reads). DOCUMENTED order: IMM, then UEFI, then (FPGA, not present on this server), then DSA Preboot (README 1.4; S-022 p11-12). IMM must be 1.07 or later before UEFI/DSA updates (README 1.4); the changelog header says 1.14 or later (conflict 13; the installed 1.30 satisfies both). Updating to IMM 1.30 requires a current level of 1.10 (YUOO57H) or later, otherwise "the system will not power on correctly" (fixed in 1.31) (README 1.4/changelog). After downgrading from 1.22 to an earlier version the IMM must be reset to factory defaults (changelog header); 1.09 to 1.10 enforces alpha and numeric passwords or may need a reset to defaults (changelog); moving from below 1.05 to 1.05 or later reverts alert recipient e-mails and DST (README, S-022 p9). When down-levelling below 1.07 from 1.07/1.08, AC power must be removed before a server reboot (README 1.2). Intel C-state erratum: README 1.4 says 32-bit Linux (command-line updates); S-022 p10 says Linux or VMware. Updates through AMM, BoMC or the IMM web/CLI are not affected (both). Never power off during "Secure Region Update in Progress" (CRTM update after a UEFI update, S-022 p10). Updates with BoMC, UXSPI, AMM or in-band individual packages take at least 17 minutes (S-022 p9).

UpdateXpress System Pack Installer / Bootable Media Creator preferred (S-022 p6). Web interface: Firmware Update, then Restart IMM; UEFI and DSA updates need the server powered on and no IMM restart (S-020 p123-124). CLI: update -i <TFTP_IP> -l <file> (S-020 p153). Flash package: <package>.bin -s, -x <path> to extract, iflash options --package --user --password --unattended --force --backup --no-reboot --silent (README); iflash64 strings additionally show --reboot, --tftp [port], --disable-imm-lan, --kcs and a password-file option (EXTRACTED). In-band updates need LAN over USB enabled and drivers; if disabled, use the web update (S-022 p8, p11; S-020 p32, p129). Windows: when the current IMM is below 1.12, updating to 1.14-1.30 adds up to 10 minutes and to 1.30 or later up to 20 minutes of iflash pre-check wait (changelog header).

The gap is documented in docs/X3650M3_FIRMWARE_HISTORY.md. From 1.30 an update to 1.55 passes the 1.10 floor. Fixes after 1.30 include 1.32 (SSH vs web lockout bypass), 1.40 (backup failover on corruption), 1.42 (SHA256/512), 1.44 (OpenSSL CVE-2014-0224/0076), 1.47 (POODLE CVE-2014-3566/3568), 1.49 (Logjam CVE-2015-4000), 1.50-1.53 (OpenSSL CVEs, 1.53 security headers) and 1.55 ("Fixed the OpenSLP heap-related memory corruption"; the changelog gives no CVE number, CVE-2017-17833 comes from the security bulletin cited in docs/X3650M3_FIRMWARE_HISTORY.md). S-023 (2011-10-10) states that for new 2011 systems individual iflash packages, IMM CLI and SNMP updates would be unsupported and the web update emergency-only (UXZ packaging), and that pre-2011 systems are not affected. This unit's board dates from Nov 2011 while the model shipped earlier. Resolved (CANDIDATE, strong): the transition does not apply. S-023 (sources/text/S-023 lines 151-154): "This affects all new systems being shipped in 2011 that include an IMM. Older systems that shipped before 2011 will not be affected and refreshes to older systems will not be affected"; the 7945 is a pre-2011 machine type whose 2011 models are a refresh ("Models announced February 2011", S-001 TIPS0805), and IBM still shipped IMM 1.55 (2018) for it as a self-extracting iflash package with iflash/iflash64 (EXTRACTED, firmware/ibm/imm/1.55-yuooh5a). See conflict 5.

This server is the Proxmox host that runs the agent and the lab. An IMM flash, IMM reset or power action takes the lab down; any flash needs explicit owner approval and a rollback plan (docs/AGENT.md). The IMM image itself (needed for any 1.55 update) is not available locally, and the backup bank state and jumper position are unknown (3.2), so there is no verified rollback.

DOCUMENTED: the web interface is reached by typing the IMM IP address or host name; after login a Welcome page asks for an inactivity timeout (fixed when the global login settings say so), then opens System Status (S-020 p22, printed 14). All login attempts are written to the event log (S-020 p22). DOCUMENTED: HTTP default port 80, HTTPS default 443, both changeable to 1-65535 on the Port Assignments page (S-020 p43). DOCUMENTED: the secure web server needs a certificate (self-signed or CA-signed) before SSL can be enabled; enabling or disabling the HTTPS server takes effect only after an IMM restart (S-020 p84-87, p90). Cryptography mode Basic Compatible (default) or High Security (disables SSL, TLS key at least 128 bits) applies to the HTTPS server and to Systems Director over HTTPS (S-020 p91-92). DOCUMENTED (IMM1 default): IMM.SSL_Server_Enable default value Disabled on IMM1 (Enabled on IMM2), and the HTTPS server certificate default "Private Key and Cert/CSR not available" on IMM1 (S-027 Appendix I, IMM1 column). This gives a documented reason why an IMM1 that was never configured has no working TLS on 443.

entries.h: 6. Serial over LAN and serial redirection

entries.x: DOCUMENTED (S-020 p41): the IMM provides two serial ports for redirection. On System x, COM1 is used for IPMI Serial over LAN and is configurable only through IPMI; COM2 is used for serial redirection through Telnet or SSH, is not IPMI-configurable and on rack servers is internal with no external connector. Both use 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit; baud 9600, 19200, 38400, 57600, 115200 or 230400. DOCUMENTED (S-002 p32, printed 18): the rear serial connector is shared with the IMM; the IMM can take control of it for text console redirection and SOL. DOCUMENTED (S-020 p42-43): console 1 in the CLI starts redirection; all COM2 traffic goes to the Telnet/SSH session; the exit key sequence returns to the CLI ("ESC Q" example, press Esc then q). Up to two Telnet sessions can view a redirected port concurrently. DOCUMENTED: the Serial Port web page sets the COM2 baud rate and the CLI mode (EMS-compatible keystrokes or user-defined keystrokes) (S-020 p41-42); CLI portcfg -b -climode and srcfg -exitcliseq (S-020 p147-148). Exit key default changed to "^[(" in 1.19 (changelog, included in 1.30); S-027 section 3.10 also gives default "^[(" and baud 115200 (IMM2 document, consistent). S-020 p148 example shows "^[Q". MEASURED (cli_settings lines 14-19): portcfg -b 115200, -climode 2 (CLI with user-defined keystroke sequences); srcfg -entercliseq ^[(. The sequence equals the documented default; the option is named -entercliseq on 1.30 but -exitcliseq in S-020 p148 (I-11). DOCUMENTED (i

entries.p: IMM 1.30 Web UI and WS-Man API
IMM 1.30 Web UI and WS-Man API
entries.x: The IMM 1.30 web UI is a frameset application written in JavaScript. Almost every page reads and writes IMM state through WS-Management custom operations: the client downloads six WSDLs at login and turns every WSDL operation into a global JavaScript function top.<Operation>(input, callback) (EXTRACTED, home_imp.js:161-231). Besides /wsman, the client uses a small set of plain HTTP endpoints for the session (/session/*), file transfer (/br/*, /certs/*, /spevents.elg), the KVM launcher (/kvm/*) and a few helpers (section 4.4).

entries.x: EXTRACTED: read directly from a file served by the IMM firmware and stored in the repository (UI code and the WSDL documents). The UI code is part of the firmware image, so its content is treated like extracted firmware content. EXTRACTED states what the client code does or what the WSDL declares, not what the server enforces. Since 2026-10-21 EXTRACTED also covers the IMM 1.10 and 1.55 firmware root file systems (web tree, lighttpd config, mod_wsman and handler libraries; captures/2026-10-21_imm_rootfs_unknown_extracts.txt); facts taken from those images are applied to the installed 1.30 only as CANDIDATE unless the 1.30 copy was compared. DOCUMENTED: vendor document, cited through docs/X3650M3_IMM_INTERFACES.md where the citation already exists. CANDIDATE: inference, with the reason given. UNKNOWN: not established. "NOT TESTED" marks request shapes in section 9 that were never sent. Values quoted from wsread are MEASURED; the meaning of a numeric code is EXTRACTED when a stored UI file maps it to a display text (file:line given), otherwise the raw value is given and its meaning is UNKNOWN.

entries.p: IMM 1.30 Web UI and WS-Man API
IMM 1.30 Web UI and WS-Man API
entries.x: Endpoint: POST <scheme>://<host>/wsman (home_imp.js:51, 207). The WSDL soap:address is the literal "No Target Adress" in every WSDL (WSDL, element service/port), so the client overrides it with wsmanURI. HTTP headers: Content-Type: text/xml, Connection: close (lib/wsman/soap.js:64-66), plus session_id when the header session is used (lib/wsman/network.js:31-34) and optionally NoSessionUpdate: yes. No SOAPAction header is sent (the code is commented out, lib/wsman/WSDLOperation.js:150-154). XMLHttpRequest is asynchronous; timeout 5 * 3600 * 1000 ms, i.e. 5 hours, although the comment says 5 minutes (lib/wsman/network.js:12); up to 2 retries for HTTP status codes outside 200, 400, 401, 403, 405, 415, 404, 500 (lib/wsman/network.js:13-15, 66-71). HTTP 400 and 500 responses are parsed as SOAP faults (lib/wsman/soap.js:109-113).

entries.p: IMM 1.30 Web UI and WS-Man API
entries.x: Namespaces (lib/wsman/XML.js:19-27): SOAP-ENV = http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope, wsa = http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2004/08/addressing, wsman = http://schemas.dmtf.org/wbem/wsman/1/wsman.xsd. Header elements in this order: wsa:To (endpoint), wsa:ReplyTo/wsa:Address (anonymous role), wsman:ResourceURI, optional wsman:SelectorSet with wsman:Selector name="..." (lib/wsman/soap.js:424-438), wsa:Action, wsa:MessageID = dt:<milliseconds>. Body: one element named after the operation with xmlns = the WSDL soap:body namespace (lib/wsman/wsdl.js:171-173), and one child per input part; simple parts carry xsi:type="xsd:<type>" (WSDLOperation.js:139-144), complex parts are built from the WSDL schema. Generic custom-operation request as the client builds it (structure EXTRACTED; values are placeholders): <SOAP-ENV:Envelope xmlns:SOAP-ENV="http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope" xmlns:wsa="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2004/08/addressing" xmlns:wsman="http://schemas.dmtf.org/wbem/wsman/1/wsman.xsd"> <SOAP-ENV:Header> <wsa:To>http://<IMM>/wsman</wsa:To> <wsa:ReplyTo><wsa:Address>http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2004/08/addressing/role/anonymous</wsa:Address></wsa:ReplyTo> <wsman:ResourceURI>http://www.ibm.com/iBMC/sp/<Service></wsman:ResourceURI> <wsa:Action>http://www.ibm.com/iBMC/sp/<Service>/<Operation></wsa:Action> <wsa:MessageID>dt:<ms></wsa:MessageID> </SOAP-ENV:Header> <SOAP-ENV:Body> <Operation xmlns="http://www.ibm.com/iBMC/sp/<Service>" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLS

entries.x: Path Port Through [remote-access service] IMM CLI over SSH, then console 1 (COM2 / ttyS1) 22/tcp Browser-rendered SSH will not work: [remote-access service] supports only curve25519 / ECDH key exchange there, while the IMM offers only group1/group14/group-exchange-sha1 and an ssh-rsa 1024 host key (MEASURED, docs/X3650M3_IMM_ARCHITECTURE.md lines 254-258). A client-side [remote-access service] access ssh ProxyCommand relays TCP and can work with legacy OpenSSH options (CANDIDATE). IPMI SOL, ipmitool -I lanplus -C 3 ... sol activate (COM1 / ttyS0) 623/udp not via a public hostname; WARP private routing with UDP is untested (CANDIDATE). SOL is enabled with forced encryption (MEASURED); use cipher suite 3. Recommended (CANDIDATE): a small always-on Debian jump host on the LAN, reached with [remote-access service] Access SSH (browser-rendered SSH is fine for a modern host); from it run legacy ssh -tt to the IMM or ipmitool SOL. The SOL client must not run on the x3650 itself: it would die with the host.

entries.h: 5. [remote-access service] connector must not live only on the Proxmox host
entries.x: MEASURED ([remote-access service]): the only [remote-access service] connector runs on the Proxmox host, so [lab-host] is unreachable whenever Proxmox is off or being reinstalled. DOCUMENTED ([remote-access service] tunnel availability / replicas): a remotely managed tunnel can run up to 25 replicas, but requests go to the closest replica with no steering, so localhost routes break on another replica. Recommended (CANDIDATE): a separate second tunnel on the jump host for out-of-band access (IMM web, IMM SSH, jump host SSH), behind the same Access policy; keep the host tunnel for Proxmox. If replicas are used instead, all routes must use LAN IPs ([lab-ip]:8006, [lab-ip]:80).

Source S-024 (UEFI intro paper, rev 1.2) unless noted; truth level DOCUMENTED. POST and boot run in four phases (S-024 p.4): (1) IMM initialization and power sequencing, (2) platform initialization, (3) pre-boot DXE, (4) BDS. The firmware follows the SEC, PEI, DXE, BDS model of the UEFI platform initialization specification (diagram S-024 p.4). The early boot code (SEC/PEI) is the contents of Capsule_P.scap in the flash package; DXE drivers and the setup engine live in FvDxe.fv and FvPlatform.fv (EXTRACTED, FORMATS doc section 6). Mapping the phase names to specific FVs follows module names (PeiMain, DxeMain, Bds) and is EXTRACTED. Two boot methods exist, UEFI and legacy (CSM via LegacyBios, EXTRACTED module); the "Legacy Only" flag and boot order storage in NVRAM are described in S-024 pp.5-9. Configuration is stored in two tiers: UEFI NVRAM variables and an IMM-held XML-modelled NVRAM; ASU covers all settings through the XML model (S-024 p.15). Adapter configuration uses HII (S-024 p.16). RAS (S-024 pp.17-18): locked CRTM region (a CRTM update is staged in flash and applied on the next boot; the power-good reset this causes is not a fault), firmware volume integrity service, power-sequence watchdog, POST watchdog (disabled by default; Setup -> System Settings -> Integrated Management Module), dual-bank ABR. Three consecutive boot failures trigger a recovery behavior whose details changed with builds of February 2010 (S-024 p.18). Corruption recovery uses a secure trusted-co

Primary and backup UEFI banks (S-004 printed p.372, PDF p.390). To restore the primary: update the primary bank, restart once on the backup, then switch back via AC removal for 15 seconds or by pressing F3 at the splash screen (S-024 p.18; S-004 p.372). Starting the backup server firmware: S-004 PDF p.517. Jumpers (S-004 Table 4, printed p.19, PDF p.37): J29 UEFI boot recovery, pins 1-2 normal (primary), 2-3 backup; J147 IMM recovery, pins 1-2 primary IMM ROM page, 2-3 secondary page. Change only with power off; no jumper behaves as 1-2. This resolves the former UNKNOWN for the IMM recovery jumper in the firmware history document. Flashing the backup bank uses iflash --backup (FORMATS doc section 8). RETAIN tip H196209: updating the UEFI backup firmware with the IMM32F method may fail (S-022 pp.15-16).

entries.h: 7.3 Flash layout and update path on the IMM (EXTRACTED, cap s8)
entries.x: NAND with UBI: kernel in UBI volumes 1/2, rootfs in 3/4, bootfs in 7/8, side = 1 or 2 ("Customer layout contains two rootfs copies in volumes 3 and 4", ifs.mtd-stage2:22; volume arithmetic in rfs.mirror:60-74). The boot side is the U-Boot environment variable bootvolume in SPI flash (rfs.mirror:79 spiutil env ibmc -r bootvolume). This is the IMM "primary/backup bank" of section 3.2 of docs/X3650M3_IMM_ARCHITECTURE.md (CANDIDATE mapping). lib/libfmp_ibmc.so: gunzips the image, writes uImage and rootfs.jffs2 to the inactive side ("/dev/mtd3 mounted, programming ubi0_2, ubi0_4"; "/dev/mtd4 mounted, programming ubi0_1, ubi0_3"; "Both NAND banks mounted, unable to update"), logs "reading uboot, no update", then moves /staging/updated/ibmc.xml to /staging/activated. U-Boot is not flashed from the package member: the rootfs carries /etc/uboot/u-boot.bin ("IMM UBoot 1.1.4 (Nov 12 2009 - 04:51:02)", sha256 38100997...) and /etc/init.d/rfs.update-uboot writes it to IMM SPI offset 0 with spiutil raw ibmc -w when its banner string differs from the one read from SPI (the script calls this string the "signature"; it is a text comparison, not cryptography). The rootfs also carries bootfs.jffs2 (identical to the package member). spiutil supports SPI parts MX25L12805D and S25FL128P and the targets ibmc|bios|fpga (cap s8). The same tool writes the host UEFI flash: libfmp_ibmc "spiutil raw bios -w -o", and in 57X /bin/uefi/burn.sh (section 7.6).

uImage identical; u-boot.bin differs in 7 bytes (build date in the banner). bootfs: 14 of 30 files rebuilt (bldinfo BUILD_NUM 43 / BRANCH prebvt_57 for 57H, BUILD_NUM 000 / empty branch for 57X; libepo.so 22066 -> 160639 B). rootfs: 2074 -> 2107 files; 33 added, all in /bin/uefi: TME132A_.001-.028 and TME145U_.029-.031 (31 x 131072 B, concatenated 0x3E0000 B, sha256 84eb93b2...), 32A_Pei_Crtm.bin (524288 B, EFI FV at 0x20) and burn.sh. 240 files changed, 229 of them only by a removed .gnu_debuglink section; real string changes in bootfs.*, etc/bldinfo, etc/rc.sysinit, lib/libcore.so (multi-node "scalability"/"complex" state machines absent in 57X) and a few platform libraries. etc/rc.sysinit in 57X adds /bin/uefi/burn.sh, which writes the host UEFI SPI flash directly with spiutil raw bios -wv: 0x400000-0x7DFFFF in 128 KiB chunks (TME132A/TME145U) and 0x380000 length 0x80000 (32A_Pei_Crtm.bin). So the 57X image reflashes the dx360 M2 primary UEFI bank, including the CRTM region, from the IMM at every IMM boot, bypassing the host-side UEFI update path. The offsets are dx360 M2 specific; whether the x3650 M3 UEFI SPI is wired the same way is UNKNOWN.

entries.h: 7.7 Vendor procedure (DOCUMENTED, X1/IMMCRTMv7.sh and X1/Instruction.pdf; cap s13, s14)
entries.x: Target: iDataPlex dx360 M2 with UEFI 45B/45C, to fix CRTM issue "TME145B" (script line 6). Prerequisites: UEFI boot recovery jumper JP2 at pins 1-2, the documented factory default account active, IMM settings at default (Instruction.pdf p1). Duration 40-50 minutes. Steps (script lines 7-19): power off, switch UEFI to the primary bank, boot to POST complete, flash imm_yuoo57x_v2.upd, wait 5 min, power off, select primary bank, power on (CRTM region rewritten to 32A, primary bank only), wait for POST, flash the normal imm_yuoo57h.upd, wait 5 min. Flash command (line 42): ./iflash --host <IMM IP> --package <file> --silent --skip_min_level --force. IPMI commands used by the script. All are listed for documentation only and must NOT be run on this host (docs/AGENT.md): the state-changing ones alter power or the boot bank, and the OEM read commands are undocumented by IBM beyond this script. Recommended order: IMM, then UEFI, then DSA Preboot (IMM 1.55 README). Full plan for this server (PLANNED, nothing executed): docs/X3650M3_FIRMWARE_UPDATE_PLAN.md. The IMM runs "a full operating system" and can take up to 17 minutes to be ready after an update (Firmware update best practices for IMMv1 systems, p.7, sources/pdf/S-022_*). IMM has primary and backup banks. A "firmware architecture change from Q3 2011" makes mixed-bank images unpredictable (https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/node/860842). Physical IMM recovery jumper: J147 (pins 1-2 primary IMM image, 2-3 secondary) and UEFI boot backup jumper J29 (S-004 Table 4, printed p.18-20; S-002 printed p.29-31; details in docs/X3650M3_IMM_ARCHITECTURE.md). This server hosts the lab (docs/AGENT.md): any update needs explicit owner approval and a rollback plan.

entries.h: 2. Delivery paths and the host OS constraint
entries.x: The IBM Linux packages install only on RHEL/SLES; the host runs Proxmox VE (Debian). Verified for the HBA package (install.sh exits 172 on other distributions, STORAGE_RAID 7.1) and DSA (TOOLS 5.7, 9.2); the same PKG SDK wrapper is used by all packages (FIRMWARE_FORMATS 3), so in-band install on the host is CANDIDATE to fail for every package. IMM web interface, Tasks -> Firmware Update (out-of-band, OS independent): documented for IMM 1.55 (README section 2.2) and UEFI 1.22 (README section 2.2). This is the planned path for IMM and UEFI. Bootable media (BoMC, RHEL-based ToolsCenter environment, TOOLS 7) or a temporary RHEL live system: planned path for M1015, HBA and NIC if they are updated at all. NOT VERIFIED on this server. DSA Preboot: iflash64 --package ... --force --bypass_platform over LAN over USB (TOOLS 5.7); needs the IMM USB network (169.254.95.x) from the running OS or boot media. NOT VERIFIED.

Owner approval of the whole plan and of a maintenance window (UEFI and storage steps reboot the host; all guests stop). Independent 5 V supply for the OOB Pi, then the deferred serial-console reboot test (STATUS Active Work), so POST/UEFI output of every reboot can be observed and logged. Backups: vzdump of all guests to a target outside the M1015 virtual disk; ASU export of all UEFI/IMM settings (asu show all, TOOLS) and the IMM configuration backup; copy of /etc/pve. SEL: it is full and logging stopped since 2025-05-05 (A-008). Save it to captures/ and clear it (owner approval), so flash success/failure events (40000023/40000024, 806f052b failover) are recorded. Physical access available for jumpers J147 (IMM recovery) and J29 (UEFI boot recovery), and for AC removal. CMOS battery: Planar VBAT is below its lower critical threshold (1.791 V on 2026-10-20, HARDWARE_COMPONENTS 12); replace the CR2032 before any step that removes AC power, or UEFI settings and clock may be lost. Record before/after versions for each step (IMM VPD via WS-Man GetVitalProductData, SMBIOS, storcli, ethtool).

entries.p: Error Codes, Event Messages and Diagnostics
entries.x: Truth level: DOCUMENTED (S-004 "POST error codes", p.274-286; same 45 codes in S-005 15th and 12th editions and in IC r_post_error_codes.html). Codes appear in the POST event log and on screen; severity can be error, warning or informational (S-004 p.274). Action text taken from the infocenter copy (same wording as S-004, cleaner extraction), condensed. Note on code formats: the x3650 M3 PDSG uses 7-hex-digit POST codes (for example 0051003). The dotted UEFI event IDs of later IBM/Lenovo servers (I.xxxxx, W.xxxxx, S.xxxxx) do not occur in any x3650 M3 source here (searched S-004, S-005, IC); do not apply them to this machine. entries.x: Truth level: DOCUMENTED (S-004 p.360; S-024 "UEFI checkpoint codes" p.27-28). S-004 contains no per-code checkpoint table for the x3650 M3; it says a checkpoint code "is either a byte or a word value produced by server firmware and sent to the I/O port indicating the point at which the system stopped during the boot block and power-on self test (POST). It does not provide error codes or suggest replacement components." S-024 (generic for IBM UEFI servers, explicitly not for the x3850 X5) gives the ranges below and warns that checkpoints are not deterministic fault indications; use light path LEDs, firmware events and the IMM log. entries.h: 13. Firmware recovery features (ABR, Nx boot failure)
entries.x: Truth level: DOCUMENTED (S-004 p.371-375). UEFI image banks and jumpers: docs/X3650M3_UEFI.md and docs/X3650M3_IMM_ARCHITECTURE.md. Feature Behavior Related codes p. Automatic boot failure recovery (ABR) If the IMM detects problems with the server firmware in the primary bank during start, the server switches to the backup bank; after recovering the primary bank, restart and press F3 at "Press F3 to restore to primary" POST 3048006 (booted backup image because of ABR), 3048005 (backup switch used); IMM 806f000f-2201xxxx (ABR Status) 375 Nx boot failure After N consecutive failed POST attempts the server reverts to default UEFI configuration and starts Setup. N = Setup -> System Settings -> Operating Modes -> POST Attempts Limit: 3, 6, 9, or 255 (= disabled) POST 3058004 (three boot failures), 3108007 (configuration restored to default) 375 Recovering the server firmware For corrupted firmware (e.g. power loss during update): in-band method = UEFI boot recovery jumper J29 (pins 2-3 boots the backup bank) or automated boot recovery, then flash the update package; out-of-band method = IMM web interface update POST 3038003, 3xx0007; IMM 806f000f-22010bxx (BIOS ROM corruption) 371-374 POST watchdog / OS watchdog Server resets if POST or OS watchdog expires (configured in Setup -> IMM settings) IMM 806f0023-2101xxxx (watchdog expired), 806f0123/0223/0323-2101xxxx (reboot / power off / power cycle by watchdog); "Intermittent problems" row 2 345

entries.x: Event IDs were first matched to section 4 by message text (CANDIDATE). The WS-Man read of 2026-10-21 returns the real 64-bit IDs (captures/2026-10-21_imm_wsman_read_inventory.txt GetEventLog, MEASURED): rows 1-4 and 9-18 match the column below exactly (for example 0x806f00091381ffff, 0x4000001900000000, 0x806f000d0400ffff, 0x806f010d0400ffff). Correction for rows 5-8 (Planar VBAT): the IMM logs entity/instance bytes 0701, not 2801: lower non-critical asserted 80010002-0701xxxx, lower critical asserted 80010202-0701xxxx, deasserted 81010002-0701xxxx and 81010202-0701xxxx; the low 16 bits vary per entry (for example 0x90b1, 0x9ca5). CANDIDATE decode: they are IPMI event data bytes 2/3 = raw trigger reading and raw threshold. Planar VBAT (sensor 0x1C) converts with M=127, R exponent -4 = 0.0127 V per count, lower critical raw 0xA5 (2.0955 V), lower non-critical raw 0xB1 (2.2479 V) (captures/2026-10-21_sdr_raw_dump.txt, MEASURED), so 0x90b1 = reading 0x90 (1.829 V) against the lnc threshold 0xB1 and 0x9ca5 = reading 0x9C (1.981 V) against the lc threshold 0xA5; both are consistent with the logged condition. IBM does not document the field. Entity 07 instance 01 is the system board, consistent with the SDR entity 7.1 of "Planar VBAT" (docs/X3650M3_SENSORS_SDR.md SC-2). For "Planar VBAT" S-004 prints the same text only under the sensor name "CMOS Battery" (docs/X3650M3_SENSORS_SDR.md SC-2). Account names are not copied here ("owner's account"). "Log" = severity letter in the IMM lo

entries.h: 3. Transports: KCS, LAN over USB, IMM external LAN, bootable media
entries.x: Details of the interfaces themselves are in docs/X3650M3_IMM_ARCHITECTURE.md sections 4.1 (KCS), 4.2 (LAN over USB), 5 (network services) and 9.3 (in-band update protocol). Tool-relevant points: KCS (in-band IPMI system interface): used by ipmitool (OpenIPMI /dev/ipmi0), by ASU as fallback or with --kcs, by iflash with --kcs. DOCUMENTED (S-026 v10.6 PDF p19): "The local connection over the KCS interface does not require authentication". Any root process on the host therefore has unauthenticated IMM access. LAN over USB (in-band virtual Ethernet to the IMM, IMM at 169.254.95.118): used by ASU (default), DSA, UXSPI, BoMC media and the iflash packages. DOCUMENTED: ASU "attempts to connect and automatically configure the LAN over USB interface if it detects that this interface is not configured" and disables it again afterwards if it was disabled before (S-026 PDF p19-20); DSA Portable and UXSPI both warn that running them changes the route table of the 169.254.95.x network and can crash cluster software (DSA 10.1 readme section 9.0; UXSPI 10.2 readme "Duplicate IP addresses when updating IMM, uEFI, and DSA"). DOCUMENTED (ASU 10.3 readme section 2.2): "there must be no network device on the system configured with an IP adress of 169.254.x.y other than the CDC Ethernet Device". The helper script that performs this host-side configuration is cdc_interface.sh (EXTRACTED: version 1.0.7 in the ASU 10.3 tgz, SHA256 8e7fe3809b102f878e68c6de1faba3477bdc2fd01dc5831ae2e9d5ac9b213457; versi

ASU modifies firmware settings from the command line: UEFI settings, IMM settings, VPD, iSCSI boot settings, and on IMM-based servers remotely over the IMM external LAN. "The ASU does not update any of the firmware code" (S-026 v10.6 PDF p7-8). It also generates/imports/exports IMM certificates and offers immapp (host power, SEL and IMM log functions, ASU 9.40+, S-026 PDF p49). entries.h: 4.4 Transport (DOCUMENTED, S-026 v10.6 PDF p19-21, p67-70)
entries.x: No connection options: ASU tries LAN over USB with the IMM default account, then falls back to KCS (needs the IPMI driver). --kcs: KCS only, no authentication. --host <IMM_IP> --user <IMM_USER> --password ... (or --password-file <file>): out-of-band over the IMM external LAN; all three required; since ASU 9.41 there is no default user/password out-of-band. The OS may be off. --noimmlancfg: skip the automatic LAN over USB configuration when the interface was configured manually. --mtsn / --net: locate an IMM on the LAN by machine type, model and serial. The IMM LAN-over-USB IP settings IMM.LanOverUsbIMMIP, IMM.LanOverUsbIMMNetmask, IMM.LanOverUsbHostIP are for IMM2 build 1AOO45F or later: "IMMV1 is not supported" (S-026 PDF p21). S-020 (IMM v1 user's guide) PDF p125: ASU 3.0.0 or later is required to manage the IMM; if LAN over USB is disabled, ASU needs IPMI device drivers.

Read-only (they read settings; save writes a local file only): ./asu64 version # read-only ./asu64 show all --kcs # read-only (all settings via KCS, no LAN-over-USB setup) ./asu64 show uEFI --kcs # read-only ./asu64 show uEFI.OperatingMode --kcs # read-only (setting from docs/X3650M3_UEFI.md) ./asu64 showvalues uEFI.OperatingMode --kcs # read-only (allowed values) ./asu64 showdefault uEFI --kcs # read-only ./asu64 showgroups --kcs # read-only ./asu64 comparedefault uEFI --kcs # read-only ./asu64 save <local_file> --kcs # read-only on the server; writes <local_file> ./asu64 nodes --kcs # read-only ./asu64 immapp powerstate --kcs # read-only ./asu64 immapp showsel --kcs # read-only ./asu64 immapp showimmlog --kcs # read-only ./asu64 show all --host <IMM_IP> --user <IMM_USER> --password-file <IMM_PASSWORD_FILE> # read-only, out-of-band ./asu64 show IMM --noimmlancfg # read-only on the IMM, but connects over LAN over USB Note: running ASU without --kcs, --host or --noimmlancfg lets it configure the LAN-over-USB interface on the host (section 3); on this Proxmox host that is a host network change (STATE-CHANGING for the host, CANDIDATE). STATE-CHANGING (owner approval required): ./asu64 set uEFI.OperatingMode "<value>" --kcs # STATE-CHANGING (UEFI setting, applies at next boot) ./asu64 setenc <setting> <encrypted_value> --kcs # STATE-CHANGING ./asu64 loaddefault uEFI --kcs # STATE-CHANGING (does not reset boot order, limitation 3) ./asu64 restore <file> --kcs # STATE-CHANGING ./as

"For IMM-based servers, after you use the ASU to change settings, you must reset the IMM before you flash new firmware. If you do not reset the IMM, the changes you made to the settings might be lost" (S-026 PDF p19). Some settings need an IMM restart to take effect or to show in the IMM web interface (S-026 PDF p7). Certificate management needs IMM level "yuoo78m or later" (PDF p7) or "yuoo71a or later" (PDF p19), conflict T-6. loaddefault does not restore the default boot order on IMM-based systems (PDF p25, limitation 3; ASU 10.3 readme 7.4). After setting IMM network settings the result may not be readable because the connection closes (limitation 8). On ESXi with IMMv1, IMM.RemoteAlertRecipient_Status.x changes do not take effect (limitation 7, list only). Windows: ASU extracts the helper driver wflash.sys (PDF p10); not relevant to the Linux host.

entries.h: 5. DSA - Dynamic System Analysis (Portable and Preboot)

entries.x: DSA collects system configuration, installed packages, kernel modules, network settings, hardware inventory (PCI, USB), light path status, service processor status and configuration, VPD and firmware levels, drive health, ServeRAID/LSI RAID configuration and the OS, RAID and service-processor event logs, plus a merged log; optional non-destructive diagnostics (-diags). Output: compressed XML and optional HTML/text (DSA 10.1 Portable readme section 1.1; S-028 9.60 PDF p13). Editions (S-028 PDF p13): Preboot Edition (embedded image or boot media, created with BoMC or flashed with a Preboot DSA update package) and Portable Edition (self-extracting executable that expands into a temporary directory and deletes it afterwards).

<dsa-package> -x -v -d <out_dir> --no-imm-lan # read-only on firmware; runs vendor code as root, writes <out_dir> <dsa-package> -v -x -i <file>.xml.gz # read-only; renders an existing collection offline (no server access) <dsa-package> --extract <dir> # read-only; unpacks the program files only <dsa-package> -diags --no-imm-lan # read-only by design ("non-destructive diagnostic tests"); still loads the server <dsa-package> --ipmi-lan <IMM_USER>:<password>@<IMM_IP> # read-only (SEL); password on the command line: avoid, not recommended here <dsa-package> -v # STATE-CHANGING for the host: may configure LAN over USB and the route table <dsa-package> -t | -upload | --update | --chkupd | -ux # network transfer to vendor/FTP or download: not allowed in this project without approval <dsa-package> fod install_imm_fod|uninstall_imm_fod ... # STATE-CHANGING (IMM Features on Demand keys) Embedded Preboot DSA: power the server off and on, press F2 at the "F2 for Dynamic System Analysis" prompt; a standalone memory test runs first, then gui or cmd (DSA 10.0 ISO readme 2.0/3.0; S-028 PDF p25). STATE-CHANGING (reboot of the Proxmox host). If both a power-on and an administrator password are set, the administrator password is required.

Default output directory /var/log/Lenovo_Support; file name <machine_type_model>_<serial_no>_<date>-<time>.xml.gz (readme 4.0/4.1). Collections contain serial numbers and configuration; review before sharing. Without --no-imm-lan, running Portable DSA "would cause cluster application such as Oracle RAC to crash unexpectedly" through 169.254.95.x route changes (readme 9.0). On "uEFI IMMv1 systems" PCI devices may lack their PCI slot mapping (SMBIOS 2.5 limitation); GPT disks show "Unknown" PartitionSubType (readme 9.0). Preboot memory test: exits at the first error; only the last loop result is passed to DSA; cannot be re-entered without a reboot (DSA 10.0 ISO readme 2.0).

Commands acquire, compare, update (S-029 10.0 PDF p40-45). S-022 (IMMv1 firmware update best practices) names UXSPI and BoMC as the preferred update tools (docs/X3650M3_IMM_ARCHITECTURE.md 9.2).

Linux: RHEL 4/5/6/7 and SLES 10/11 executables only (S-029 PDF p28-29); Windows Server 2008-2012 R2 (PDF p27). Debian/Proxmox not listed. Linux driver updates need rpm-build, perl and bash (RHEL) (PDF p29; readme 5.1). "64-bit Linux requires compat-libstdc++" to run 32-bit binaries including UXSPI (readme 5.1, rpm -qa | grep compat-libstdc++-296); libstdc++.so.6 required (readme). CANDIDATE: not usable on this host (reason: RPM-based OS detection and update packages, 32-bit dependencies, no Debian support in any local source). Not tried; no binary local.

In-band on the target OS. IMM version detection needs IPMI drivers; the IMM update itself does not (readme 5.1). IMM/uEFI/DSA updates use LAN over USB (169.254.95.118/.120) and can duplicate addresses or change routes (readme, "Duplicate IP addresses when updating IMM, uEFI, and DSA"). --remote=<address> runs compare/update on another server's OS (not the IMM); only Windows-to-Windows or Linux-to-Linux; update over remote is unattended only (S-029 PDF p38, p45). <uxspi> compare --local=<uxsp_dir> # read-only (inventory/compare); uses IPMI/LAN over USB <uxspi> acquire --local=<dir> ... # read-only on the server; downloads from the vendor (network) <uxspi> update --local=<uxsp_dir> -u # STATE-CHANGING (flashes firmware / installs drivers) <uxspi> update --remote=<os_ip> --remote-user=<user> --remote-password=<pw> ... # STATE-CHANGING on a remote OS

The Windows LSI driver is always installed even when the controller is disabled (readme 5.1). Updating the IMM from a USB key unmounts the key; do other updates first (readme). Updates via BoMC, UXSPI, AMM or individual in-band packages take at least 17 minutes; never power off during "Secure Region Update in Progress" (S-022 p9-10, via docs/X3650M3_IMM_ARCHITECTURE.md 9.1).

Creates one bootable image (CD, DVD, ISO, USB flash drive or PXE files) that bundles Preboot DSA, UXSPI and update packages (and, in older versions, ServerGuide) for selected machine types (BoMC 10.3 readme chapter 1; S-030 9.63 PDF p14-15). For diagnostic or update media "only the Linux update packages for your selected machine types are included" (BoMC 10.3 readme).

The package readme names supported Linux distributions only as "linux" builds (FIRMWARE_FORMATS 8); Debian is not mentioned in any local source.

python3 -I scripts/ibm_fw_unpack.py extract <package> <out_dir> # read-only, no vendor code executed (preferred) <package>.bin -x <path> # read-only for firmware, but executes the vendor stub (avoid; use the line above) <package>.bin -s # STATE-CHANGING (silent flash) ./iflash64 --package <file>.upd [--backup] [--no-reboot] [--kcs] ... # STATE-CHANGING (flash; --backup writes the backup bank) Caveats: update order IMM, then UEFI, then DSA Preboot; IMM must be at least 1.07 (README) or 1.14 (changelog header) before UEFI/DSA updates; wait times and the 17 to 20 minute IMM restart are in FIRMWARE_FORMATS 7 and IMM_ARCHITECTURE 9.1. --user disables KCS authentication failover (README via IMM_ARCHITECTURE 9.3). The packages cannot change UEFI settings; ASU does that (FIRMWARE_FORMATS 8). Any flash on this host needs owner approval and a rollback plan; for the IMM there is no verified rollback (IMM_ARCHITECTURE 9.5).

5.1 What the CPU can and cannot do
entries.x: Turbo: the E5606 has none (DOCUMENTED S-001; MEASURED no ida flag). The UEFI items "Turbo Mode" (uEFI.TurboModeEnable) and "Turbo Boost" (uEFI.TurboBoost) therefore have no effect on this CPU (CANDIDATE: firmware cannot enable a feature the part lacks; consistent with the absent flag). Do not spend a reboot on them. Hyper-Threading: none (DOCUMENTED + MEASURED). uEFI.ProcessorHyperThreading is irrelevant on this CPU. P-states (EIST): present and active; OS range 1197-2128 MHz (MEASURED). S-022 p.10 (DOCUMENTED): "Due to an Intel erratum, if your server is running Linux or VMware, you should disable C-States before you update UEFI, IMM, FPGA, or DSA Preboot. C-states can be returned to the original settings after the updates are complete. See RETAIN TIP H195678." Updates through the IMM web or CLI interface do not have this requirement. The IMM 1.55 README restricts it to 32-bit Linux command-line updates (conflict, section 14). Consequence: if C-states are enabled (R-C5), any in-band (Proxmox-side) firmware update must be preceded by disabling them again, or the update must be done through the IMM web interface. Expected benefit of enabling C-states: lower idle power on a host that measured 80 W at capture time (CANDIDATE; reason: S-035 describes C-states as halting the core clock in idle and C1E as an automatic voltage/frequency reduction; the size of the saving on this machine is not measured). Expected cost: small wake-up latency (CANDIDATE, S-035 C-state text). No number is claimed.

entries.h: 6.1 Current state and the cost of it
entries.x: One 8 GB RDIMM in DIMM03 uses one of the CPU's three DDR3 channels (MEASURED + DOCUMENTED, docs/X3650M3_MEMORY.md sections 3, 9). Two consequences (CANDIDATE, from the topology): memory bandwidth is limited to one channel, and 7.7 GiB is the total for host, ZFS ARC (if a pool exists), KSM and all guests.

Speed = min(CPU limit, DIMM rating, DPC limit). The E5606 limit is 1066 MHz (S-001 model 7945-22x row). 1 DPC and 2 DPC give 1066 MHz on this CPU under both S-001 and S-002; 3 DPC gives 800 MHz. Fill order per CPU for performance: 3, 6, 9 (one DIMM per channel), then 2, 5, 8, then 1, 4, 7. Connectors 10-18 need the second CPU. RDIMM and UDIMM never mixed. 1.5 V and 1.35 V RDIMMs may be mixed on Xeon 5600; all then run at 1.5 V. Mirroring needs identical pairs (3+6 first), sparing needs three identical DIMMs (3, 6, 9). After any DIMM change: disconnect power, wait 10 seconds; refit the DIMM air baffle.

entries.h: 10.2 Why the UEFI update matters for a KVM host
entries.x: Microcode in UEFI (EXTRACTED, docs/X3650M3_UEFI.md section 9): 0x206C2 is 0x15 in UEFI 1.14 and 0x1F (2018-05-08) in 1.22; the OS runs 0x14 (MEASURED). UEFI 1.18 (D6E160A, Critical) incorporated microcode M03206C2_0000001A "to address Intel Erratum BD132 and AAK167 for System Resets with 32-bit (PAE Enabled) Guest OS and VT FlexPriority enabled" (RETAIN H21370) and BD131 for X5675/X5687/X5690 (H21371) (UEFI .chg, DOCUMENTED). The CPU reports the flexpriority VMX feature (MEASURED). A Proxmox host running 32-bit PAE guests on microcode 0x14 is therefore exposed to that documented reset erratum (CANDIDATE). Update 2026-10-21: in the Intel Xeon 5600 specification update (323372-017US, Feb 2015, Table 3 and p.53) the 5600 erratum is BD132 "Virtual-APIC Page Accesses With 32-Bit PAE Paging May Cause a System Crash" (AAK167 is the Xeon 5500 twin); its only stepping column is B-1 (= CPUID 0x206C2, this CPU), marked "No Fix" with a BIOS workaround possible (DOCUMENTED). IBM ships the workaround as microcode 0x1A in UEFI 1.18, so 0x1F (UEFI 1.22 or intel-microcode) also carries it (CANDIDATE). Today no VM runs on the host: qm list shows none, and the two guests are LXC containers ([lab-guest] agent-claude2 and CT 529823444, both amd64; pct config, 2026-10-21, MEASURED), so no 32-bit PAE guest is exposed at present. UEFI 1.21 (CVE-2017-5715) and 1.22 (CVE-2018-3639/3640) add Spectre-era microcode (DOCUMENTED). The OS currently reports Spec store bypass "Vulnerable" (MEASURED). MDS stay

entries.h: 10.3 Order (DOCUMENTED, S-022 pp.11-12; IMM 1.55 README section 1.4)
entries.x: Prerequisites on this host: backup (R-A6), new CMOS battery (R-C1), SEL saved and cleared (R-C2), maintenance window agreed with the owner (the agent container goes down), IMM reachable out of band. IMM first, then UEFI, then FPGA (not present), then DSA Preboot. UXSPI/BoMC are the preferred tools and may choose their own order. "It is recommended that all firmware including IMM, UEFI, FPGA and DSA Preboot are updated together as a matched set" (S-022). Adapter firmware (M1015, HBA, Broadcom) afterwards (CANDIDATE: not part of the documented system-firmware order). Constraints and risks (DOCUMENTED unless marked): The IMM 1.55 package is now in the repository (firmware/ibm/imm/1.55-yuooh5a, analysed in captures/2026-10-21_imm_upd_1.55_analysis.txt), so the documented order could start; no update is executed (D-006, owner decision 2026-10-21). UEFI 1.22 alone is permitted by its prerequisites (IMM 1.07 per README, YUOO57H = 1.10 per XML; the installed 1.30 satisfies both, docs/X3650M3_UEFI.md section 10), but it breaks the matched-set recommendation. Decision for the owner. In-band updates from Linux: disable C-states first (Intel erratum, S-022 p.10; section 5.3). Updates through the IMM web interface or CLI are not affected. They need LAN over USB for in-band packages (S-022 p.8). An update takes at least 17 minutes; the IMM can need up to 17 minutes to be ready after its own update (S-022). After a UEFI update, reboot to let the CRTM update run; "Do not power off the system

Load microcode from the OS at boot: Debian package intel-microcode (Proxmox VE 8 is Debian 12 based; package in the non-free-firmware component) installs files under /lib/firmware/intel-ucode/ and the early initramfs loader applies them at every boot (CANDIDATE: agent knowledge of Debian packaging, not in the repository sources). The host's Debian APT lines list only main contrib (MEASURED, C-BA lines 92-94), so the package is not installable from the configured sources (CANDIDATE consequence: it lives only in non-free-firmware). Adding non-free-firmware to those lines is a persistent change of the host's package sources and needs owner approval; it is a precondition of R-B1. Revision for 06-2c-02: Intel's public microcode repository file intel-ucode/06-2c-02 is rev 0x1F dated 2018-05-08, signature 0x206C2, pf mask 0x03 (includes this CPU's platform ID 0; processor_flags 0x1, MEASURED); Debian re-enabled 0x206C2 in intel-microcode 3.20180807a.2 (Intel GitHub Intel-Linux-Processor-Microcode-Data-Files; Launchpad bug 1795594, DOCUMENTED). That the bookworm package ships this same 0x1F file is CANDIDATE (package not inspected; no newer Intel release exists for this signature). As it is 0x1F it gives the same CPU fixes as UEFI 1.22 without touching flash. It does not update the UEFI code itself (CRTM, IMM interface fixes, VLAN, memory reference code). Reversible by removing the package and rebuilding the initramfs. Needs a host reboot to take effect, hence owner approval.

x3650m3-kb is an engineering knowledge base for the IBM System x3650 M3 server (machine types 7945, 4255 and 7376). It collects every hardware and software detail that public vendor documents, firmware packages and read-only measurements of one reference unit can support. The aim is to understand the management side of the platform (IMM, UEFI, IPMI and the firmware update path) well enough to operate and optimise an owned server safely. Experiments and live tests are limited to the owner's own machine. The project started on 2026-10-19. The knowledge lives in a private Git repository; this site is a sanitized, read-only rendering of it (decision D-007, 2026-10-21).

Vendor documents first. IBM and Lenovo manuals, product guides, readmes and changelogs were collected and given source ids (S-001 to S-038). Every fact names its source and page. See the Reading guide. Firmware packages analysed offline. Packages were downloaded with their checksums and unpacked by the project's own Python tools without running any vendor code (EXTRACTED facts). See the Firmware guide and Tools guide. Read-only measurements. Inventory, sensors, logs and settings of the reference unit were captured with commands that do not change state (MEASURED facts). State-changing actions such as firmware updates require the owner's explicit approval and are documented as plans, not results. Truth levels. Every statement is marked DOCUMENTED, EXTRACTED, MEASURED, CANDIDATE or UNKNOWN. Nothing is invented to fill a gap; open questions are listed in each volume.

Path Content docs/ The knowledge volumes (X3650M3_*.md, published here) and project documents (requirements, architecture, decisions, test plan, changelog) sources/ Source catalog (S-xxx ids), the Lenovo download catalog, an archived IBM InfoCenter subset for the 7945 and a static copy of the IMM 1.30 web interface firmware/ IBM and Lenovo firmware packages with source URLs and SHA256 sums (the site shows metadata only) captures/ Read-only command outputs from the reference unit (not published as files) scripts/ Python analysis tools: package unpacker, IMM .upd and UEFI volume parsers, read-only CIM and WS-Man inventory clients, download and archive helpers tests/ unittest suite for the scripts, run in CI on every push site/ Hand-written pages, the file catalog and the publication rules of this site The file catalog in the Catalogs section describes every directory and file in more detail.

The site is generated by scripts/build_library.py from the repository: python3 -m pip install -r requirements-site.txt python3 scripts/build_library.py --out _site Volumes are rendered from docs/X3650M3_*.md, these pages from site/pages/*.md, and the catalogs of firmware, sources, scripts and files from repository metadata. Every string passes through a sanitizer with the rules in site/publish.json, and a leak check scans the output; if it finds anything, the build fails and its output is deleted. Internal documents (operating notes, the owner's security assessment and working logs) are never published.

Firmware binaries and vendor document files. Only names, versions, dates, sizes and SHA256 checksums appear. Addresses, host names, network layout, serial numbers, UUIDs and MAC addresses of the owner's equipment. The owner's security assessment and anything that would describe weaknesses of a specific live system. Vendor-published CVE lists per firmware level are public information and remain. Credentials of any kind. The IBM factory defaults quoted in the guides come from IBM's own documentation.

IBM and Lenovo documents, firmware and web interface files remain the property of their owners. This site publishes original analysis, short quotations for reference and metadata about vendor files; it does not redistribute vendor binaries. IBM, System x, ServeRAID, Lenovo and XClarity are trademarks of their respective owners. The site is an independent engineering reference and is not affiliated with or endorsed by IBM or Lenovo.

One reference unit was measured; other configurations are described from vendor documents only. Vendor documents of this era are partly withdrawn; some were read from archives (see the Reading guide). Firmware updates and other state-changing tests were not performed; their outcome is described as PLANNED or CANDIDATE where it appears at all.
Short answers with the truth level of the underlying fact. Follow the links for sources; when an answer says UNKNOWN, the library has no source for it.
The IBM System x3650 M3, machine types 7945, 4255 and 7376 (DOCUMENTED). Most analysis was done on one reference unit of type 7945. See System at a glance and Hardware 3.1.

Intel Xeon 5500 (Nehalem-EP) and Xeon 5600 (Westmere-EP), one or two sockets, linked by QPI to an Intel 5520 IOH (DOCUMENTED). Xeon 5600 support arrived with UEFI 1.06 (D6E145C). See System architecture 3 and Firmware history.

entries.h: How much memory can it hold, and how fast does it run?
entries.x: Eighteen DDR3 DIMM slots, nine per processor; speed falls with DIMMs per channel (1 DPC up to 1333 MHz, 3 DPC 800 MHz), and the processor's own memory limit also applies (DOCUMENTED). Only the slots of an installed CPU can be used. See Memory 4.2 and Memory 5.1.

entries.h: Can I mix RDIMMs and UDIMMs?
entries.x: No; the rules forbid mixing registered and unbuffered DIMMs (DOCUMENTED). See Memory 4.1.

entries.h: Why does the server not beep?
entries.x: The vendor states that the server does not use beep codes; it reports through light path LEDs, the checkpoint display, POST error codes and the IMM event log (DOCUMENTED). See Error codes 8 and the Troubleshooting guide.

entries.h: What are the J29 and J147 jumpers for?
entries.x: J29 forces the backup UEFI bank and J147 the backup IMM bank (pins 2-3) for recovery after a failed flash (DOCUMENTED). See Hardware 4.1 and the UEFI guide.

entries.h: What is the default IMM login and address?
entries.x: Per IBM documentation: user USERID, password PASSW0RD (with a zero), and a static fallback address 192.168.70.125 when DHCP fails (DOCUMENTED). Change the password on first use. See the IMM guide and IMM architecture 6.

entries.h: Is the IMM the same as IMM2 or XClarity Controller?
entries.x: No. The x3650 M3 has the first-generation IMM (IMM v1, builds YUOOxxx); IMM2 and XCC belong to later servers and their manuals do not apply directly (DOCUMENTED). See Firmware history, naming.

entries.h: Which interfaces does the IMM offer?
entries.x: Web (HTTP/HTTPS), legacy CLI over SSH and Telnet, IPMI over LAN (RMCP/RMCP+) and in-band KCS, SOL, SNMP, CIM, WS-Man, SLP and LAN over USB (DOCUMENTED and MEASURED). See IMM interfaces 2 and the IMM guide.

entries.h: How do I get a remote graphical console?
entries.x: Remote presence (KVM and virtual media) needs IMM Premium, enabled by the Virtual Media Key option (DOCUMENTED). Without it, use the serial paths (SOL or CLI serial redirection). See IMM architecture 7 and IMM interfaces 6.

entries.h: How do I read the IMM event log from the command line?
entries.x: Use the CLI command readlog over SSH (five entries per call), or ipmitool sel list for the IPMI SEL (DOCUMENTED, MEASURED). See IMM architecture 10.

entries.h: What does an IMM event id such as 80010202-2801xxxx mean?
entries.x: The first part identifies the event class and sensor type, the second the entity and instance; the decoding is inferred from IPMI sensor events (CANDIDATE) and each id is listed with its vendor text. See Error codes 3 and the Troubleshooting guide.

entries.h: Why does the IMM web interface feel slow or need old Java/ActiveX?
entries.x: The IMM v1 web UI is a frame-based JavaScript application that calls WS-Man for nearly every page; remote control used Java or ActiveX clients (EXTRACTED, DOCUMENTED). See IMM web API 3 and Firmware history.
IMM 1.55 (YUOOH5A), UEFI 1.22 (D6E164A) and Preboot DSA 9.53 (DSYTC5F) are the newest levels found (DOCUMENTED); see Firmware history, latest available and the Firmware guide.

entries.h: In what order should firmware be updated?
entries.x: The IMM 1.55 readme recommends IMM first, then UEFI, then Preboot DSA, and some UEFI levels require a minimum IMM level (for example UEFI 1.08 needs IMM YUOO73M) (DOCUMENTED). The IMM can take up to 17 minutes to be ready after an update. See Firmware history, update order and IMM architecture 9.1.
With care: going below IMM 1.22 (YUOO84C) requires a factory reset of the IMM configuration (DOCUMENTED). See Firmware history.

entries.h: Why does a UEFI update need a second reboot?
entries.x: The CRTM (boot block) cannot be written while in use; it is staged and applied at the next start (DOCUMENTED). See UEFI 3 and the Firmware guide.

The analysed IMM v1 .upd images (1.10 and 1.55) carry MD5/CRC checks, not a cryptographic signature; the UEFI image has an RSA2048-SHA256 trailer on its early boot code (EXTRACTED). See Firmware formats 7.4 and Firmware formats 6.

entries.h: Where can I still download the packages?
entries.x: The IBM delivery servers and the Lenovo support catalog (Data Center Support, "DS" document ids) still served the packages in 2026-10; some need an IBM ID at Fix Central (MEASURED at download time). See Firmware history, open items and About.

entries.h: Which CPU security fixes need a UEFI update?
entries.x: UEFI 1.21 carries Spectre v2 microcode and 1.22 the Speculative Store Bypass microcode (DOCUMENTED). See UEFI 9.

entries.h: Can I use OneCLI instead of ASU, DSA and UXSPI?
entries.x: Whether OneCLI supports this machine type is UNKNOWN in the library; ASU, DSA, UXSPI and BoMC are the documented tools. See Tools 8.

entries.h: How do I change UEFI settings without a monitor?
entries.x: With ASU (asu show, asu set uEFI.<name> <value>) in-band over LAN over USB, or remotely against the IMM address; changes take effect at the next boot (DOCUMENTED). See Tools 4 and UEFI 7.

entries.h: How do I get a text console on the host serial port?
entries.x: Enable console redirection in UEFI and attach through IPMI SOL (COM1) or the IMM CLI console 1 command (COM2) (DOCUMENTED). See the UEFI guide and IMM interfaces 6.

entries.h: Which operating mode should I pick?
entries.x: Acoustic, Efficiency, Performance and Custom presets change speed, C-state and turbo settings; their exact effect on power is CANDIDATE on this platform. See UEFI 6 and Power and thermal 9.

entries.h: What does LAN over USB do and why is it there?
entries.x: It is a USB network link between host and IMM (IMM side 169.254.95.118) used by ASU, DSA and firmware updates (DOCUMENTED). See IMM interfaces 10.
Press F2 at POST to start Preboot DSA from IMM flash, or run DSA Portable from the OS (DOCUMENTED). See Tools 5 and the Troubleshooting guide.

entries.h: Which RAID controller is typical and what can it do?
entries.x: The ServeRAID M1015 (LSI SAS2008): RAID 0, 1 and 10, RAID 5/50 with an upgrade key, no cache and no battery (DOCUMENTED). See Storage 4.1 and Storage 9.

entries.h: Which tool manages the M1015 from Linux?
entries.x: StorCLI (the newest Linux build found is 1.16.14); the IBM 6Gb SAS HBA uses SAS2IRCU and SAS2FLASH instead (DOCUMENTED). See Tools 10 and Tools 11.

entries.h: Can I flash IT firmware over IR on the SAS HBA?
entries.x: The bundled SAS2FLASH refuses to cross the IT/IR personality and refuses NVDATA downgrades (EXTRACTED). See Storage 7.1.

entries.h: Can I trust every statement here?
entries.x: Each statement carries a truth level: DOCUMENTED and MEASURED facts are strongest, CANDIDATE is reasoning that still needs proof, UNKNOWN means no source. See the Reading guide.

entries.h: Does the library contain firmware binaries?
entries.x: No. It publishes analysis, metadata and checksums only; vendor documents and firmware remain the property of IBM and Lenovo. See About.

Every firmware component of the x3650 M3 (IMM, UEFI, DSA Preboot, ServeRAID M1015, 6Gb SAS HBA, BCM5709) - versions, latest levels, package formats, how updates are delivered and the documented risks. The x3650 M3 carries six independently updated firmware images that matter in practice. This guide explains what each one is, which versions exist, how IBM packaged them, how an update reaches the hardware and what the vendor documents warn about. It describes; it does not recommend an update for any particular machine. The authoritative detail is in the volumes linked in each section, chiefly Firmware history, Firmware formats and the firmware update plan (a PLANNED, never executed plan for the reference unit, useful as a worked example).

Every IBM package of this era follows the same pattern (EXTRACTED, Firmware formats 3, 4): File Role <name>.bin / <name>.exe PKG SDK self-extractor: ELF i386 (Linux) or PE32 (Windows) stub + unzip + image.tar (the .upd) + image.zip (flash tools, wrapper scripts) + imgboot.cfg, located by a 20-byte trailer of five little-endian sizes <name>.xml CIM-XML descriptor (supported machine types, prerequisites, CRC, release date) used by UpdateXpress <name>.chg Change history <name>.txt Readme: install methods, prerequisites, known issues <build>.upd Flash payload: tar with a descriptor (oem_ibm.xml, ibmc.xml or dsap.xml) and the images Packages can be unpacked without running them, either with -x <dir> on the vendor wrapper (executes vendor code) or statically with scripts/ibm_fw_unpack.py extract (reads bytes only) (Firmware formats 9).

The first-generation Integrated Management Module end to end - hardware and firmware internals, every interface (web, CLI, IPMI, SOL, SNMP, CIM/WS-Man, SLP, LAN over USB), users, Standard versus Premium, banks and recovery. The Integrated Management Module (IMM) is the service processor of the x3650 M3. It is the first IMM generation ("IMM v1"); the x3650 M4 and later use IMM2 and XClarity Controller, which behave differently. This guide walks through the IMM from silicon to user interfaces. Authoritative detail: IMM architecture, IMM interfaces and the IMM web API.
