After login the IMM v1 web interface offers (S-020 Table 2): System Status, Virtual Light Path, Event Log, Vital Product Data, Power/Restart, Remote Control (Premium), PXE Network Boot, Firmware Update, System Settings, Login Profiles, Alerts, Serial Port, Port Assignments, Network Interfaces, Network Protocols, Security, Configuration File, Restore Default Settings, Restart IMM, and on some systems Scalable Partitioning and Service Advisor (CANDIDATE: not applicable to the x3650 M3). Each link with its CLI and ASU equivalent is mapped in IMM interfaces 3.2. On IMM1 the HTTPS server is disabled by default and no certificate exists until one is generated or imported; enabling HTTPS needs a certificate and an IMM restart (DOCUMENTED, S-020 pp.84-90, S-027 Appendix I). Cryptography mode "High Security" disables SSL and weak keys. The 1.30 web client is analysed file by file in the IMM web API volume: the login is a POST /session/create, after which six WSDLs are downloaded and every WSDL operation becomes a JavaScript function. The six WS-Man services are Monitors (17 operations), Tasks (20), iBMCControl (54), iBMCNWProtocol (13), ServiceAdvisor (21) and Scalability (8); 53 are read operations by name (EXTRACTED, classification CANDIDATE).

Commands present in the 1.30 help (MEASURED): ?, clearcfg, clearlog, clock, console, dhcpinfo, dns, exit, fans, gprofile, help, history, identify, ifconfig, ipsec, ldap, ntp, passwordcfg, portcfg, power, readlog, reset, resetsp, slp, srcfg, ssl, syshealth, temps, timeouts, update, usbeth, users, volts, vpd. Some commands documented in S-020 (for example portcontrol) belong to later firmware. Display forms are read-only; forms with options change state; clearlog, clearcfg, reset, resetsp, power and update change state (IMM interfaces 4.2, 4.3).

The IMM implements IPMI 2.0 with manufacturer ID 2 (IBM) and product ID 220; it supports the sensor device, SDR repository, SEL, FRU inventory, IPMB event receiver/generator and chassis functions; mc getsysinfo and DCMI discovery are not implemented (MEASURED on the reference unit). Authority levels map to IPMI privileges: Supervisor to Administrator, Read Only to User (DOCUMENTED, S-020 pp.35-36). IBM OEM commands exist but are not documented in the local sources (IMM interfaces 5.5). The sensor repository is decoded in Sensors and SDR.

entries.h: Serial over LAN and serial redirection
entries.x: On rack System x servers COM1 carries IPMI Serial over LAN and is configured only through IPMI; COM2 is the internal port for serial redirection through the CLI (console 1); both are 8N1 at 9600-230400 baud. The rear serial port is shared with the IMM (DOCUMENTED, S-020 pp.16, 41; S-002). The UEFI side needs console redirection enabled (uEFI.RemoteConsoleRedirection, uEFI.SerialPortSharing, uEFI.SPRedirection and the COM settings); see the UEFI guide.

The IMM presents an internal Ethernet device (USB 04b3:4010 "IBM RNDIS/CDC ETHER") to the host. The IMM side is 169.254.95.118/16 (S-020 p.129); the documented Linux host address is 169.254.95.130 in S-020 and 169.254.95.120 in IBM's cdc_interface.sh (recorded conflict). From IMM 1.15 a DHCP server on the link is documented. ASU, DSA, UXSPI, BoMC media and the iflash packages use this link; they may reconfigure the host's network to do so, which IBM's own readmes warn can disturb cluster software. Disabling "commands on USB interface" stops in-band flash and ASU over this path (ASU can still use KCS) and should be paired with disabling the OS watchdogs (IMM architecture 4.2, IMM interfaces 10).

Up to 12 login profiles shared by web, CLI, SNMPv3 and IPMI; IPMI user ID 1 is the null user, IPMI ID n+1 is login ID n; login IDs at most 16 characters (DOCUMENTED, S-020 pp.33-38). Authority levels: Supervisor, Read Only, Custom (with rights such as User Account Management, Remote Console, Remote Power/Restart, Clear Event Logs, Adapter Configuration Basic/Advanced, Networking and Security). Login order options: local only, LDAP only, local first then LDAP, LDAP first then local. IPMI never uses LDAP. Account security levels Legacy, High and Custom control lockout, web inactivity timeout, password history and age. Factory defaults (DOCUMENTED in IBM readmes and S-020): login ID USERID with password PASSW0RD (zero, not the letter O); if no DHCP answer is received, the IMM uses the static address 192.168.70.125. Changing the default credentials is the first step of any deployment. Password-rule details differ between sources (recorded conflict, IMM architecture 6).

Standard IMM includes remote power control, serial redirection, SOL, LAN over USB, LDAP, SNMP, ASU, remote firmware update, OS watchdogs and embedded DSA. Premium (the IBM Virtual Media Key, option 46C7526, FRU 46C7528, installed in a dedicated system-board slot with AC removed) adds remote presence (graphical KVM), operating-system failure screen capture and remote disk. No firmware change is needed for the upgrade (DOCUMENTED, S-020 pp.11-13, 114; S-001 Table 18). Remote presence supports up to 1280x1024 at 75 Hz per S-001 and S-020, 1600x1200 per S-002 and S-004 (recorded conflict). The 1.30 Remote Control page asks the IMM for a license status before showing the KVM launcher (EXTRACTED) (IMM architecture 7).

The IMM keeps two logs: the IPMI SEL (all BMC, POST and SMI events; fixed size; when full, new entries are not written) and the IMM event log (a filtered subset of IMM, POST and SMI events as text messages with event ids, plus IMM-internal events such as logins and network changes). The CLI readlog shows five entries per call, newest first; the web Event Log page sorts and filters; clearlog clears. An IMM reported its event log capacity as 1500 records through CIM (MEASURED on the reference unit). Decoding is covered in the troubleshooting guide (IMM architecture 10).

Two banks. Primary and backup (secondary) IMM firmware pages; jumper J147 pins 1-2 normal, 2-3 boot the backup page; change only with power removed (DOCUMENTED, S-004 Table 4). On flash (EXTRACTED, IMM 1.10): NAND managed by UBI with two sides (kernel volumes 1/2, rootfs 3/4, bootfs 7/8); U-Boot at offset 0 of an SPI flash selects the side via an environment variable and can fall back to TFTP; updates write the inactive side and a mirror job later copies the running side. How J147 maps to this is UNKNOWN (IMM architecture 3.2). Automatic failover to the backup bank on corruption exists from IMM 1.40 (DOCUMENTED, changelog). Event ids: 40000023/40000024 flash success/failure, 4000002a firmware mismatch, 806f052b-2101xxxx IMM firmware failover (DOCUMENTED, S-004). Resetting: Setup -> System Settings -> Integrated Management Module offers "Reset IMM to Defaults" and "Reset IMM" (about 4 minutes); removing AC for 45 s resets the IMM (DSA I2C test note). Configuration backups exclude the Security page settings and the SSH server key (DOCUMENTED, S-020). Known defect band: IMM 1.30-1.32 can fail over unexpectedly and stop (RETAIN H206034, fixed in 1.33); see the firmware guide.

The IMM offers an OS watchdog and a loader watchdog (server timeouts) that require the in-band USB interface; a missed check restarts the server. A POST watchdog (disabled by default) is configured in UEFI Setup. When no IBM in-band agent runs in the OS, the IMM may keep showing the server state "Booting OS" (S-020 p.111 lists "Booting OS or in unsupported OS"); on the reference unit this state is MEASURED while the OS runs, the cause is CANDIDATE (IMM architecture 4.5).

Still UNKNOWN in the volumes: which IMM bank is active and what level the backup holds (no read-only query known), the exact flash part numbers, the IBM OEM IPMI command set, the wire protocol ASU uses out-of-band to an IMM1, and the SoC identity beyond the PCI ID (IMM architecture 13).

How to read the library - truth levels with examples, source ids, page conventions, how measurements and firmware analysis were done, and the limits of the evidence. The library is written so that every statement can be traced back to evidence. This page explains the labels you will meet on every page, how the evidence was produced, and what the evidence cannot tell you.

The levels are defined in docs/AGENT.md of the repository and used identically in every volume. A table row inherits the level stated for its table; a sentence states its own. Level What it means Typical evidence Example from the library DOCUMENTED A vendor document says so. Guide title, edition, source id S-xxx and page or section. "This server does not use beep codes for server status" (S-004 printed p.274), Error codes 8. EXTRACTED Read from a vendor firmware binary or package by offline analysis. Package path, SHA256, offset or member name, tool command. UEFI 1.22 ships microcode revision 0x1F for CPUID 0x206C2, UEFI 9. MEASURED Captured from the reference unit with a read-only command; the raw output is kept under captures/. Capture file and line. The reference unit reports IPMI version 2.0, manufacturer ID 2 (IBM), product ID 220, IMM architecture 2. CANDIDATE An inference that is plausible but not proven; the reason is always written next to it. Reasoning from other facts. The IMM SoC is the Vitesse VSC452 (reason: PCI ID plus driver names in the firmware), IMM architecture 3.1. UNKNOWN No source in the repository establishes it. - Which IMM flash bank is active cannot be read with any known read-only query, IMM architecture 3.2. Additional status words: PLANNED marks an action described but not executed (for example the firmware update plan). The x3650 M3 uses the first-generation IMM ("IMM v1", firmware builds named YUOOxxx). Later System x servers use IMM2 (M4/M5 generation, builds 1AOO/TCOO) and then XClarity Controller. Commands, settings, ports and defaults differ between them. The volumes import nothing from IMM2 or XCC without marking it, and several vendor sources (for example S-027, an IMM2 configuration guide) are used only for their explicit IMM1 notes (IMM interfaces 1). The same caution applies to error codes: the dotted UEFI event ids (I.xxxxx, W.xxxxx) of later servers do not exist on this machine (Error codes 6).

All MEASURED facts come from one reference unit and were captured with commands that read state without changing it: in-band IPMI over the KCS interface with ipmitool (sensors, SDR, SEL, FRU, LAN and SOL configuration), display-only commands of the IMM legacy CLI (vpd, syshealth, ifconfig, users, ssl, readlog ...), OS-side inventory (dmidecode, lspci, lsusb, ACPI tables, /proc and /sys, EFI variables, smartctl), storcli show commands for the RAID controller, run from a temporary copy and removed afterwards, ASU show all over KCS, and the parameterless "Get" operations of the IMM WS-Management and CIM interfaces, network service discovery of the IMM (port scans, SLP discovery, protocol probes). A small number of captures record configuration changes that the owner requested (for example creating a virtual disk or enabling serial console redirection). Those are explicitly labelled STATE-CHANGING in the volumes and are not presented as observations of an untouched machine. No firmware was flashed, no IMM was reset and no log was cleared to produce any fact in this library.

Vendor packages (IMM, UEFI, DSA, RAID, HBA and NIC firmware) were downloaded from IBM and Lenovo, hashed and then analysed offline as untrusted data: the project's own parsers (scripts/ibm_fw_unpack.py, scripts/uefi_fv.py, scripts/imm_upd.py) read bytes and write extracted copies to a scratch directory; they never execute anything from a package, Python was run in isolated mode (python3 -I) so that files inside a package cannot be imported, results (module lists, setup forms, ASU setting tables, microcode lists, file system contents, version strings) are recorded with the package SHA256 and the command used (Firmware formats 9). The library publishes analysis and metadata only, not the vendor binaries (see About).

One machine. Measured values come from a single unit with a sparse configuration (one CPU, one DIMM). Fan speeds, power readings, sensor sets and PCIe topology will differ on other configurations. Firmware gaps. The IMM 1.30 image installed on the reference unit was not obtainable, so IMM internals are EXTRACTED from 1.10 and 1.55 images and only bracketed (CANDIDATE) for 1.30 (Firmware formats 7.8). Static analysis only. Behaviour that can only be seen by running an update, resetting the IMM or rebooting is marked NOT VERIFIED; the update plan in the volumes is PLANNED and was deliberately not executed. Withdrawn product. Some vendor pages are gone (for example the ServerProven list, S-037); some downloads need an IBM ID. Gaps are recorded as UNKNOWN rather than filled from memory. Conflicting sources. Vendor documents disagree in places (maximum memory, memory speed at two DIMMs per channel, part numbers, remote-presence resolution). Both values are kept; see Knowledge base 4.1. Not advice. Guides describe what the documents and analysis show. They are not a recommendation to change a particular machine; flashing firmware or changing settings carries the risks described in the firmware guide.

The management, diagnostic and update tools of the x3650 M3 era - ASU, DSA, UXSPI, BoMC, OneCLI, iflash, ipmitool, StorCLI, SAS2IRCU/SAS2FLASH - what each is for, how it reaches the hardware, and which commands only read and which change state. IBM shipped the x3650 M3 with the "ToolsCenter" family of utilities; Lenovo later replaced most of them with OneCLI. This guide explains what each tool is for, which transport it uses, which operating systems it supports, and - most importantly - which commands only read and which change the machine. The detail, local package paths and hashes are in the Tools volume. Conventions: read-only = the command reads state (it may write a local output file); STATE-CHANGING = it changes settings, firmware, logs, power or the host's own network. Command syntax below is DOCUMENTED unless marked CANDIDATE. Placeholders such as <IMM_IP> stand for your own values; never put passwords on a command line.

Most confusion with these tools comes from how they reach the IMM (Tools 3): Transport Used by Notes KCS (in-band IPMI, /dev/ipmi0) ipmitool, ASU (--kcs or fallback), iflash (--kcs) "The local connection over the KCS interface does not require authentication" (S-026): any root process can talk to the IMM LAN over USB (IMM at 169.254.95.118) ASU (default), DSA, UXSPI, BoMC media, iflash packages The tools may configure the host's USB network interface and routes themselves (IBM's cdc_interface.sh); IBM readmes warn about duplicate 169.254.x addresses and cluster software IMM external LAN ASU --host, ipmitool -I lanplus, web, SSH CLI, SNMP, CIM Works with the host OS down; needs IMM credentials Bootable media Preboot DSA, BoMC images Runs on the server instead of its OS; needs a reboot Practical rule drawn from the volume: an in-band tool run that touches LAN over USB should be treated as STATE-CHANGING for the host's networking (CANDIDATE), which is why --kcs is used for read-only ASU work.

Purpose. ASU reads and writes every setting that UEFI exposes through its setup XML (uEFI.*, iSCSI.*, PXE.*) and the IMM settings (IMM.*), saves and restores whole configurations, manages IMM certificates and has an immapp helper for power state and logs (S-026). Version 3.0.0 or later is required for the IMM (S-020); the newest local copy is ASU 10.3 (Lenovo package DS118233). Setting names and defaults: UEFI guide, UEFI Appendix A. Connection options (S-026 printed pp.16-17): no option = LAN over USB with default settings, then KCS; --kcs = KCS only, no authentication; --host <IMM_IP> with credentials = out-of-band over the IMM LAN. Read-only: asu64 show all --kcs # every setting asu64 show uEFI.OperatingMode --kcs # one setting asu64 showvalues uEFI.OperatingMode --kcs asu64 showdefault uEFI --kcs asu64 comparedefault uEFI --kcs asu64 save <local_file> --kcs # writes a local file only asu64 immapp powerstate --kcs asu64 immapp showsel --kcs STATE-CHANGING: asu64 set <setting> <value> --kcs # applies at the next boot for uEFI settings asu64 loaddefault uEFI --kcs # does not reset the boot order on IMM systems asu64 restore <file> --kcs | replicate <file> --kcs | batch <file> --kcs asu64 set IMM.LanOverUsb Disabled --kcs # documented to need --kcs, the link drops during the set asu64 rebootimm --kcs # IMM restart asu64 immapp poweronos|poweroffos|rebootos --kcs asu64 immapp clearsel|clearimmlog|clearalllog --kcs Caveats (DOCUMENTED, Tools 4.6): after changing settings with A

Purpose. DSA collects configuration, installed software, hardware inventory, light path status, service processor configuration, VPD and firmware levels, drive health, RAID configuration and the OS, RAID and IMM event logs into one compressed XML (with optional HTML), and runs non-destructive diagnostics (S-028; DSA 10.1 readme). Editions. Preboot is embedded in IMM flash and started with F2 at POST (or booted from media); the newest package is 9.53 DSYTC5F (Tools 5.7). Portable is a self-extracting executable (newest local 10.1 DSALA5Q) built only for RHEL, SLES, VMware 4.x and Windows; its behaviour on other distributions is UNKNOWN. <dsa-package> -x -v -d <out_dir> --no-imm-lan # read-only collection (runs vendor code as root) <dsa-package> -diags --no-imm-lan # non-destructive diagnostics; still loads the server <dsa-package> -v -x -i <file>.xml.gz # render an existing collection offline <dsa-package> -v # without --no-imm-lan: may reconfigure LAN over USB and routes <dsa-package> -t | -upload | --update # network transfers to the vendor or FTP Caveats: collections contain serial numbers and configuration, review before sharing; without --no-imm-lan the readme warns that 169.254.95.x route changes can crash cluster software (Tools 5.6). DSA messages are decoded in the troubleshooting guide.

UXSPI (UpdateXpress System Pack Installer) applies UpdateXpress System Packs and individual updates; commands compare (read-only inventory), acquire (download), update (STATE-CHANGING). It supports RHEL 4-7, SLES 10/11 and Windows; --remote works only OS-to-OS of the same type. IBM names UXSPI and BoMC the preferred update tools for IMMv1 systems (S-022, S-029) (Tools 6). BoMC (Bootable Media Creator) builds one bootable CD, DVD, ISO, USB or PXE image with Preboot DSA, UXSPI and the update packages for selected machine types. Creating media touches no server; booting it on the server is STATE-CHANGING. Media need UEFI or UEFI-and-legacy boot mode; BoMC needs LAN over USB enabled to compare levels (S-030; BoMC readmes) (Tools 7). OneCLI (Lenovo XClarity Essentials) replaces ASU, DSA and UXSPI on Lenovo systems. No OneCLI package appears in the Lenovo catalog for machine type 7945; support for IMM v1 is UNKNOWN. In-band it documents creating a temporary BMC account over KCS (CANDIDATE reading: state-changing) (Tools 8).

Every IBM IMM, UEFI and DSA package carries iflash (i386) and iflash64 (x86-64) inside its image.zip, started by the linwrap wrapper. Options (package readme): --package, --user, --password / --password-file, --unattended, --force, --backup (secondary bank), --no-reboot, --skip_min_level, --silent; strings also show --kcs, --tftp and --disable-imm-lan (EXTRACTED). Running a package with -x <dir> only extracts it, but it still executes the vendor wrapper; scripts/ibm_fw_unpack.py extract extracts without running anything. Every flash is STATE-CHANGING (Tools 9, Firmware formats 8).

The generic IPMI client works in-band (OpenIPMI driver, /dev/ipmi0) and out-of-band (-I lanplus, RMCP+ on 623/udp) (Tools 12). Read-only: ipmitool mc info ipmitool fru print ipmitool sdr elist full ipmitool sdr type list ipmitool sensor ipmitool sel info ipmitool sel elist ipmitool chassis status ipmitool lan print 1 ipmitool channel info 1 ipmitool user list 1 ipmitool sol info 1 ipmitool mc getenables ipmitool mc guid ipmitool sel save <file> ipmitool -I lanplus -H <IMM_IP> -U <user> -f <password_file> sdr elist full STATE-CHANGING: ipmitool chassis power off|on|cycle|reset|soft ipmitool chassis bootdev <device> ipmitool chassis policy always-on|previous|always-off ipmitool sel clear ipmitool mc reset warm|cold # IMM restart, up to 17-20 minutes ipmitool lan set 1 ... # can cut out-of-band access ipmitool user set|enable|disable|priv ... ipmitool sensor thresh <sensor> ... ipmitool sol activate # opens the console session ipmitool raw <netfn> <cmd> ... # treat as state-changing unless known to be a read Not implemented by IMM v1 (MEASURED): mc getsysinfo and dcmi discover return "Invalid command". Use -f <file> or -E rather than -P <password>, which exposes the password in the process list (CANDIDATE good practice).

StorCLI manages MegaRAID controllers including the ServeRAID M1015 (Lenovo packages up to 1.16.14; the readme lists the M1015 46M0831). The storcli64 binary is static x86-64 and ran read-only from a temporary copy on the reference unit (MEASURED). Read-only: storcli64 show, /c0 show all, /c0/vall show all, /c0/eall/sall show all, /c0 show patrolread, /c0 show cc, /c0 show eventloginfo, /c0/fall show. STATE-CHANGING: add vd, del, set on controllers, VDs or drives, foreign import, and download file= (firmware) (Tools 10). WebBIOS (Ctrl+H, or the UEFI HII browser on UEFI boots) and MegaRAID Storage Manager are the interactive alternatives (Storage 8). SAS2IRCU 20.00.00.00 is the IR/volume utility for LSI SAS2 HBAs; its readme lists the "6Gb SAS HBA (46M0907)" and requires the mpt2sas module. The binary is static i386. Read-only LIST, 0 DISPLAY, 0 STATUS and state-changing CREATE, DELETE, HOTSPARE, LOCATE follow common LSI usage and are CANDIDATE syntax only. SAS2FLASH (the SAS2 firmware flasher) has no standalone package in the repository; version 20.00.00.00 is bundled inside the IBM HBA 1.20 package, where its strings refuse to flash IT over IR firmware (and the reverse) and refuse NVDATA downgrades (EXTRACTED; -listall is its read-only listing, every flash is STATE-CHANGING) (Tools 11, Storage 7.1).

How to diagnose an x3650 M3 - where errors are reported, light path LEDs, POST codes, IMM event ids, the SEL, sensors, DSA Preboot, and a symptom-to-source table. The x3650 M3 reports problems through several channels that complement each other. This guide shows which channel to read first and how to decode what it shows. The complete catalogues (655 IMM event ids, 45 POST codes, 63 DSA messages, symptom tables) are in the Error codes volume; everything there is DOCUMENTED from the Problem Determination and Service Guide (S-004, 16th edition) and cross-checked against the archived infocenter. Actions marked "trained service technician only" in S-004 are kept that way.

Channel What it holds How to read it Light path diagnostics panel LEDs per subsystem; stay lit only while AC is connected Slide the blue release latch on the operator information panel left and pull the panel out System-board and riser LEDs Error LEDs next to DIMMs, CPUs, fans, PCI slots; 12 V power-channel LEDs A-E and AUX; IMM heartbeat Cover removed, AC connected Checkpoint display Two-digit code of the last boot step reached; not an error code Light path panel POST event log The three most recent POST error codes F1 Setup -> System Event Logs -> POST Event Viewer System event log (SEL) All BMC, POST and SMI events; fixed size; when full, new entries are NOT written F1 Setup -> System Event Log; ipmitool sel elist; DSA ("IPMI event log") IMM event log Filtered text messages with event ids, plus IMM events (logins, network changes) IMM web Event Log; CLI readlog; DSA ("ASM event log") DSA log Merge of SEL, IMM log and OS logs plus test results DSA Preboot (F2 at POST) or DSA Portable Beep codes None: "This server does not use beep codes for server status" - Source: S-004 pp.28-31, 274, 360; S-020 pp.97-98 (Error codes 2, 8). Severities: Information (no action), Warning (possible problem) and Error (may need action); the IMM web log marks Warning "W" and Error "E" (S-004 p.31, S-020 p.99).

The panel (S-004 Fig 4) has three rows of LEDs, a Remind button, a recessed NMI button, the checkpoint display and a recessed Reset button (Hardware 6.2): Row LEDs 1 OVER SPEC, LOG, LINK, PS, PCI, SP 2 FAN, TEMP, MEM, NMI 3 CNFG, CPU, VRM, DASD, RAID, BRD What each LED means (DOCUMENTED, S-004 pp.363-367; Error codes 9.1): LED Meaning First place to look (none, system-error LED lit) Undiagnosable error or IMM failure System event log in Setup BRD System board: battery, missing PCI riser assembly, or failed voltage regulator Board LEDs; CMOS battery; riser in connector 2 CNFG Configuration error, together with CPU or MEM Mismatched CPUs; invalid DIMM population; option ROM out of resources CPU CPU failed, or invalid CPU configuration with CNFG CPU LEDs on the board DASD Drive failed or missing Drive status LEDs; backplane FAN Fan failed, slow or removed (TEMP may also light) LED next to the fan connector LOG An error was written to the event log IMM and system event logs MEM Memory error, or invalid configuration with CNFG DIMM LEDs; logs NMI Non-maskable interrupt System event log OVER SPEC Shutdown due to overload on a power channel Power-channel LEDs A-E/AUX; supply LEDs PCI Error on a PCI bus; an LED lights at the failing slot Slot LEDs; remove adapters one at a time PS Supply failed; PS+CNFG = mixed supply types Supply LEDs SP IMM failed AC power cycle; IMM firmware TEMP Temperature over threshold Logs, room temperature, vents, fans LINK, RAID, VRM Reserved - The Remind b

entries.h: Step 2: the checkpoint code (if the server stops in POST)
entries.x: A checkpoint code shows where boot stopped, not what failed (S-004 p.360). Ranges (S-024, generic IBM UEFI): 0x00-0x0F CPU init, 0x10-0x1F PEI, 0x20-0x9E DXE, 0x9F POST complete, 0xA0-0xAF QPI, 0xB0-0xBF memory init, 0xE0-0xE5 processor or bus failure, 0xE8 no memory, 0xED invalid mixed DIMMs, 0xEE invalid DIMM population. A per-code list for this server is UNKNOWN (Error codes 7).

POST codes are seven hex digits (for example 0051003) and appear on screen and in the POST event log. The dotted codes of later servers (I.xxxxx, W.xxxxx) do not apply. Groups (structure CANDIDATE, inferred from the table): Prefix Area Examples 001xxxx Microprocessor 0011002 CPU mismatch; 001100A microcode update failed 005xxxx Memory 0051003 uncorrectable DIMM error; 0058007 unsupported population; 00580A5 mirror failover 006xxxx CMOS / battery 0068002 CMOS battery cleared 201xxxx PCI / PCIe 2018001 PCIe uncorrected error; 2018002 option ROM resource allocation failure 303xxxx-313xxxx Firmware, configuration, boot 3048006 booted backup image (ABR); 3058004 three boot failures; 305000A RTC date/time incorrect 380xxxx IMM communication 3808000 IMM communication failure; 3808004 IMM system event log full 381xxxx CRTM 3818001-3818007 CRTM update and capsule signature errors 382xxxx AEM 3828004 power capping disabled Full list with actions: Error codes 6.

IMM messages carry an id such as 806f010c-2001xxxx. S-004 lists the ids but not their structure; the decode below is CANDIDATE, inferred from all 655 ids and consistent with the IPMI sensor types measured on the reference unit (Error codes 3): Field (AABBCCDD-EEFFxxxx) Meaning AA 80 assertion, 81 deassertion, 40 IMM-internal event BB IPMI event/reading type: 01 threshold, 03 discrete, 07 generic severity, 0b redundancy, 6f sensor-specific CC Offset within the type (for thresholds 02 = lower critical going low, 09 = upper critical going high) DD IPMI sensor type (01 temperature, 02 voltage, 04 fan, 07 processor, 08 power supply, 0c memory, 0d drive slot, 0f firmware, 10 event logging, 23 watchdog) EE Entity (03 CPU, 04 drive, 07 system board, 0a power supply, 1d fan, 20 DIMM, 22 system firmware, 28 battery) FF Instance (DIMM n = 20nn, drive n = 04nn) Worked example: 80010202-2801xxxx = assertion (80), threshold (01), lower critical going low (02), voltage (02), battery entity (28), instance 01: the CMOS battery is below its lower critical threshold. The documented user response is to replace the battery (Hardware 12). The 64 condensed user responses (A01-A64) are in Error codes 5; the full message list in Error codes 4. Useful IMM-internal ids: 40000023 / 40000024 firmware flash success / failure, 4000002a firmware mismatch, 40000029 SSH login failures; 806f052b-2101xxxx IMM firmware failover; 806f000f-2201xxxx ABR status.

entries.h: Step 5: the SEL and the IMM event log
entries.x: The SEL is small (512 entries on the reference unit) and does not overwrite: once full, new hardware events are lost from it. Save it and clear it when the IMM logs the "more than 75 percent full" event (S-004 p.28). POST code 3808004 also reports a full log. Clearing is a state change: ipmitool sel save <file> first, then clear only deliberately. The IMM event log keeps recording while the SEL is full and holds human-readable messages; readlog pages through it five entries at a time. Its capacity was reported as 1500 records on the reference unit (MEASURED). The two logs share a time base but the IMM log is a filtered subset: it omits firmware-progress events, for example (IMM architecture 10).

ipmitool sensor and ipmitool sdr elist show current readings and thresholds. Threshold names differ between interfaces (IPMI lnc/lcr/lnr, CLI "warning / soft shutdown / hard shutdown"); discrete sensors show state bytes that need the reading-type tables to decode (Sensors and SDR 3, 6). The reference unit's SDR holds 135 sensor records; the full verbose dump with entities, masks and hysteresis is in Sensors and SDR 13. Example thresholds on that unit: ambient warning 38 deg C, soft shutdown 41, hard shutdown 45; Planar VBAT lower critical 2.095 V.

Press F2 during POST to start DSA Preboot (stored in IMM flash). Tests end Passed, Failed or Aborted; view results with view in the CLI or the "Diagnostic Event Log" in the GUI. Messages have the form CCC-TTT-xxx: CCC is the component (089 CPU, 166 IMM I2C, 201/202 memory, 215 optical, 217 SAS/SATA drive, 405 Broadcom Ethernet ...), TTT 8xx = aborted, 9xx = failed (CANDIDATE from the state column); each maps to an action D01-D28 (Error codes 10, 11). DSA Portable runs the same inventory from a supported OS (tools guide).

entries.h: Good practice drawn from the documents
entries.x: Read before changing: logs, LEDs and sensors are all readable without side effects; clearing a log, resetting the IMM or reseating parts is not. After installing or removing a DIMM, disconnect power and wait 10 seconds before restarting (S-004). Before replacing the CMOS battery, record UEFI settings (ASU save), because they may be lost. Check for a newer firmware level or a RETAIN tip when an action says so; IBM's actions often start with "update the firmware" (see the firmware guide for what that involves).

The x3650 M3 system firmware - POST flow, the F1 Setup tree, ASU setting names, operating modes, console redirection, flash banks and recovery jumpers, microcode and what changed between releases. The x3650 M3 was among IBM's early UEFI servers: its system firmware is UEFI 2.1 compliant, keeps a legacy BIOS compatibility module for older operating systems and adapters, and shares its configuration with the IMM. This guide summarises the UEFI volume; package and image formats are in the firmware guide and Firmware formats 6.

DOCUMENTED (S-024, IBM's "Introducing uEFI-Compliant Firmware" paper) unless noted (UEFI 2): IMM initialisation and power sequencing. The IMM must be up before the host can start; this is why the power button only works some minutes after AC is applied. Platform initialisation (SEC and PEI phases): CPU, QPI and memory initialisation. The early code is the Capsule_P.scap image of the flash package (EXTRACTED). Pre-boot DXE: drivers, option ROMs, the Setup engine (FvDxe.fv, FvPlatform.fv, EXTRACTED). BDS (boot device selection): UEFI boot entries or legacy boot through the CSM (LegacyBios module, EXTRACTED). Configuration lives in two tiers: UEFI NVRAM variables, and an XML-modelled store held by the IMM that ASU uses for every setting (S-024 p.15). Adapters present their configuration through HII forms (S-024 p.16). RAS features of the firmware (S-024 pp.17-18): a locked CRTM region (a CRTM update is staged and applied at the next boot; the resulting power-good reset is expected), firmware volume integrity checks, a power-sequence watchdog, a POST watchdog (off by default), dual banks with automatic bank recovery, and a recovery behaviour after three consecutive boot failures. The update capsule carries an RSA2048-SHA256 signature trailer (EXTRACTED); POST codes 3818005-3818007 report invalid CRTM capsule signatures (DOCUMENTED, S-004). Boot progress is reported as checkpoint codes on the light path panel display: 0x00-0x0F CPU init, 0x10-0x1F PEI, 0x20-0x9E DXE, 0x9F POST com

Press F1 at the prompt. With an administrator password set, entering it gives the full menu; otherwise a limited menu is shown (DOCUMENTED, S-002 pp.158-162). The tree (UEFI 4): System Information: System Summary, Product Data (and, from the extracted forms, Reference Code Level and Processor Details Summary). System Settings: Processors, Memory, Devices and I/O Ports, Power, Operating Modes, Legacy Support, Integrated Management Module (POST watchdog, Reboot System on NMI, Commands on USB Interface Preference, Network Configuration, Reset IMM to Defaults, Reset IMM), Adapters and UEFI Drivers, Network, Storage, Video. Date and Time, Start Options, Boot Manager (boot order, driver options, one-time boot, WOL boot options, time-out, console options, COM attributes), System Event Logs (POST Event Viewer, System Event Log, clear), User Security (power-on and administrator passwords), Save Settings, Restore Settings, Load Default Settings, Exit Setup. The extracted HII forms of 1.22 contain 27 formsets; the platform module alone renders about 1478 lines of options. Highlights per page (EXTRACTED, UEFI 5): Page Main options Processors Turbo Mode, Turbo Boost, C-states, C-state limit, Hyper-Threading, VT, Data Reuse, QPI link speed, active cores Memory Memory speed, 2DPC maximum frequency, LV-DIMM power, channel mode (Independent / Mirroring / Sparing), spare error threshold, socket / channel / rank interleave, patrol and demand scrub, page policy, data scrambling, thermal mode Ope

Every Setup option that has an ASU name can be read and written from the OS or over the network with the Advanced Settings Utility (see the tools guide). The setting list comes from an XML document inside FvOem_Ibm.fv: in UEFI 1.22 it defines 209 top-level settings (202 uEFI.*, 4 iSCSI.*, 3 PXE.*) and 147 sub-settings; the ASU name is <config mriName>.<setting mriName>, not the XML ID attribute (EXTRACTED; naming rule DOCUMENTED by S-026) (UEFI 7; the full table is UEFI Appendix A). Selected settings and their 1.22 defaults (EXTRACTED; * = default): ASU name Meaning Values uEFI.OperatingMode Operating mode Custom Mode*, Acoustic, Efficiency, Performance uEFI.TurboModeEnable / uEFI.TurboBoost Turbo Disable / Power Optimized, Traditional uEFI.ProcessorCcxEnable CPU C-states Disable* uEFI.PackageCState C-state limit ACPI C2* in 1.22 (ACPI C3 in 1.14) uEFI.ProcessorHyperThreading Hyper-Threading Enable* uEFI.ProcessorVmxEnable / uEFI.VTdSupport VT-x / VT-d Enable / Disable uEFI.DdrSpeed / uEFI.QPISpeed Memory / QPI speed Max Performance*, Minimal Power, Power Efficiency uEFI.MemoryChannelMode Memory mode Independent*, Mirroring, Sparing uEFI.PatrolScrub / uEFI.DemandScrub Scrubbing Disable / Enable uEFI.PostAttemptsLimit Nx boot failure 3*, 6, 9, Disable uEFI.PowerState Power restore policy Restore*, Always Off, Always On uEFI.EnergyManager AEM power capping Enable* uEFI.WatchdogTimerUefi POST watchdog Disable* uEFI.LimitBootAttempts Limit boot attempts (1.22 only) Enable* uEFI.T

The Operating Modes page sets several parameters at once (EXTRACTED; the mode-to-column assignment is CANDIDATE because the tool does not render the IFR OR operators) (UEFI 6): Parameter Acoustic Efficiency Performance Custom (default) Memory speed Minimal Power Power Efficiency Max Performance selectable (Max Performance) Processor performance states Enabled Enabled Disabled selectable (Enabled) C1 Enhanced mode Enabled Enabled Disabled selectable (Enabled) QPI link speed Minimal Power Minimal Power Max Performance selectable (Max Performance) Turbo mode Disabled Disabled Enabled selectable (Disabled) Help text: "Efficiency: Highest performance per watt. Acoustic: Lower acoustic level and lowest power. Performance: Highest performance. Custom: Customized settings." A non-Custom mode makes the individual questions read-only. The thermal and power effect is discussed in Power and thermal 9.

To see POST, Setup and the boot manager over IPMI Serial over LAN or the IMM CLI console 1, IBM's ASU example for IMM servers enables uEFI.RemoteConsoleRedirection, uEFI.SerialPortSharing, uEFI.SerialPortAccessMode (Dedicated; RETAIN H205981 warns that a session is lost after an IMM reset in Shared mode), uEFI.SPRedirection, VT100 terminal emulation and "active after boot" on the COM ports (DOCUMENTED, S-025). All of these default to Disable / ANSI in 1.22 (EXTRACTED). On rack servers COM1 carries SOL and COM2 serves CLI redirection (DOCUMENTED, S-020). After such a change on the reference unit the ConIn/ConOut NVRAM variables listed both UARTs at 115200 8N1 VT100 (MEASURED); serial output during POST itself was NOT VERIFIED (UEFI 12.3). The system summary is always shown on text remote consoles regardless of Quiet Boot (S-024).

Two banks. The UEFI flash has a primary and a backup bank (DOCUMENTED, S-004 p.372). SMBIOS OEM strings report the current bank and the backup level ("$CF Current UEFI Flash Bank", MEASURED on the reference unit). Restoring the primary after a bad update: update the primary bank, boot once from the backup, then switch back by removing AC for 15 seconds or pressing F3 at the splash screen (S-024 p.18; S-004 p.372). Jumper J29 (UEFI boot recovery): pins 1-2 normal, 2-3 load the backup page; change only with power off. Adapters on riser 2 may have to be removed to reach it (S-004 pp.372-373). Automatic boot failure recovery (ABR): POST 3048006 = booted the backup image because of ABR; 3048005 = the backup switch was used. Nx boot failure: after 3, 6 or 9 failed POST attempts (Setup -> Operating Modes -> POST Attempts Limit) the firmware loads defaults and enters Setup (POST 3058004, 3108007). Clear CMOS: switch SW3-1 (power off, cover removed) resets UEFI settings (Hardware 4). Backup-bank flashing: iflash --backup; RETAIN H196209 warns that updating the UEFI backup with the IMM32F method may fail (UEFI 3).

Each UEFI image carries six Intel microcode updates (Nehalem-EP 0x106A4/0x106A5 and Westmere-EP 0x206C0/1/2). For the common Westmere-EP stepping 0x206C2: 1.13 ships revision 0x14, 1.14 ships 0x15 (2011-08-26), 1.22 ships 0x1F (2018-05-08); the Spectre v2 and SSB mitigations arrived with 1.21 and 1.22 (EXTRACTED / DOCUMENTED). An OS can also load newer microcode at boot without flashing (discussed in Optimization 10.4) (UEFI 9).

Comparison Modules Notable setup changes Where 1.13 -> 1.14 150 of 178 modules changed - UEFI 8.1 1.14 -> 1.22 154 differ at file level; 21 of 312 leaf files change substantively Memory Refresh and Static Driver Impedance added; IMM VLAN support and VLAN ID added; Limit Boot Attempts added; C-state limit default ACPI C3 -> C2; Power C-States form default flips UEFI 8 1.13 -> 1.22 154 changed, 24 identical; 40 leaf files substantive as above plus microcode 0x14 -> 0x1F UEFI 8.1 The full version history is in the firmware guide and on the timeline.
The meaning of the protected="true" attribute on 134 settings, the per-code checkpoint table, the exact mapping of the IMM-side settings store and some form-to-XML mappings remain UNKNOWN (UEFI 11).

Build the public static "library" website of the x3650m3-kb repository (GitHub Pages). Usage: python3 scripts/build_library.py --out _site [--repo .] [--config site/publish.json] [--strict-links] Dependency: Python-Markdown (pinned in requirements-site.txt); everything else is the standard library. Output: OUT/index.html (redirect to library/), OUT/library/index.html (home shelf) and every page below OUT/library/. All links are relative, so the site works under /x3650m3-kb/ on GitHub Pages and from file://. No external fonts, scripts or stylesheets are referenced. Inputs (repository paths): docs/X3650M3_*.md knowledge volumes (except the never-published list in site/publish.json) publish.json about_docs selected project documents ("About this project") site/pages/*.md hand-written pages with front matter (title, section, order, summary) firmware/**/SHA256SUMS firmware package catalog (metadata only, binaries are never published) firmware/ibm/SOURCE.txt download origin, installed and latest markers of the IBM packages sources/SOURCES.md source document catalog (S-xxx ids); sources/lenovo/CATALOG.md summary scripts/*.py, scripts/*.sh tools reference (parsed with ast, never imported or executed) git ls-files + site/catalog/files.tsv repository file index (path<TAB>description, longest prefix) Publication safety: every string that reaches the output passes through scripts/library_sanitize.py with the rules of site/pub

Offline analysis of IBM System x firmware update packages (x3650 M3 era). Python 3 standard library only. The tool never executes anything contained in a package; it only reads bytes and writes extracted copies to an output directory. Supported formats (see docs/X3650M3_FIRMWARE_FORMATS.md): * IBM "PKG SDK" self-extractors (.bin = ELF i386 stub, .exe = PE32 stub) with a 20-byte trailer of five little-endian uint32 element sizes: [stub, unzip utility, image.tar (.upd), image.zip, imgboot.cfg] * The .upd update image (POSIX tar: oem_ibm.xml + <build>.tar.gz) * The CIM-XML package descriptor (.xml, class IBMPSG_SystemUpdateElement) * UEFI PI firmware volumes (FFS v2), EFI/Tiano and LZMA compressed sections, Intel microcode updates, PCI option ROMs, HII string and form packages. Sub-commands: info identify a package and list its elements (JSON) extract extract all elements of a package into a directory xml parse a CIM-XML package descriptor into JSON upd parse a .upd image (tar with oem_ibm.xml) into JSON fv list firmware volumes / FFS files of a file microcode list Intel microcode updates found in a file hii dump HII string packages and the reconstructed setup form tree baseline write a text fingerprint of a UEFI package into a directory diff compare two baseline directories
[not published]

Offline parser for IBM IMM v1 firmware update images (.upd, "YUOO" builds). Python 3 standard library only. The tool never executes anything contained in an image; it only reads bytes and, for `jffs2 --outdir`, writes copies of regular files (mode 0644, no symlinks or device nodes) into an output directory. Format (EXTRACTED from IMM 1.10 YUOO57H / YUOO57X, see docs/X3650M3_FIRMWARE_FORMATS.md section 7): * outer GNU tar: ibmc.xml (IBMBladeCenterFWUpdFmt descriptor) + ibmc.tgz * ibmc.tgz: gzip tar with u-boot.bin, uImage (U-Boot legacy image, MIPS Linux), rootfs.jffs2 and bootfs.jffs2 (big-endian JFFS2) * integrity: XML <md5chk> = MD5 of ibmc.tgz, <compressed_size> = size of the .upd file in YUOO57H (YUOO57X_v2 is one 10240-byte tar record larger), gzip CRC32, uImage header/data CRC32, JFFS2 node CRCs; no signature block was found. Sub-commands: info parse a .upd and verify md5chk, compressed_size, uImage CRCs, JFFS2 (JSON) jffs2 list (and optionally copy out) the regular files of a JFFS2 image
[not published]

Lenovo Data Center Support download catalog and fetcher for machine type 7945. Commands: catalog Fetch (or read a saved) driver-list API response and write a normalized catalog JSON plus a human-readable CATALOG.md. fetch Download catalog files into <dest>/<category-slug>/<DocId>/<filename>, verify hashes, write SHA256SUMS and SOURCE.txt per DocId directory. status Report present / missing / bad files per category. Python 3 standard library only. API notes (verified 2026-10-19): - The API answers 403 {"message":"deny access"} without a session. A GET of the HTML driver-list page with a browser User-Agent sets the cookies the API needs; the API call then needs Referer = page URL, Accept: application/json and X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest. - download.lenovo.com and delivery04.dhe.ibm.com files download without cookies. - "Size" values are rounded display strings ("323.79 MB"); they are not exact and are never used for verification. Units are interpreted as binary (1 KB = 1024 B), which is an assumption. - Many files (mostly old delivery04.dhe.ibm.com entries) carry no hash at all. - Some URLs carry a signed, expiring "__token__" query parameter (Microsoft OEM media). The token is removed from the catalog and such files are not fetched.

Sanitizer and leak gate for the public x3650m3-kb library site - Python 3 standard library only. The repository is private, the GitHub Pages library built from it is public. Every piece of text that goes into the site (rendered pages, search index, catalogs, file names) passes through this module, and the finished output tree is scanned by the leak gate before it may be published. Rules come from site/publish.json (see that file for the active rule set): remove_sections Whole sections (heading plus everything up to the next heading of the same or a higher level) of a named document: [{"file": "X3650M3_FOO.md", "heading": "11. Exact heading"}]. A configured section that is not found is reported by missing_sections() (no silent drift). remove_blocks Markdown blocks (paragraph, list item with its children, table row, heading, code fence) that match any of these patterns are dropped completely (embedded firmware credentials, live-server security findings). A rule with "require" removes a block only when the block also matches the require pattern (e.g. only MEASURED statements, not vendor documentation). UEFI firmware volume (FV), FFS file and section parser - Python 3 standard library only. Built for the IBM System x3650 M3 UEFI images (D6E1xx builds), but follows the UEFI Platform Initialization (PI) specification structures, so it works on other PI images. Commands: list Parse one or more files (raw FV, capsule, or any blob that contains FVs) and print every volume, file and leaf section (GUID, type, UI name, sizes, SHA256). extract Write every leaf section body (PE32, TE, RAW, UI, ...) and every RAW file to a new, empty output directory. Nothing is ever executed. diff Compare two images (or two directories of .fv/.scap files) module by module. microcode List Intel microcode updates found in RAW files. Input handling: - FVs are located by scanning for the "_FVH" signature at offset 0x28 of a candidate header and validating the header checksum, so capsules (.scap), whole flash dumps and single .fv files are all accepted. - A directory argument means "all *.fv and *.scap files in it, sorted by name". Decompression: - Compression section type 1 (EFI_STANDARD_COMPRESSION): the EFI (position bits 4) and Tiano (position bits 5) variants are both implemented here in pure Python; the variant whose output parses as a valid section stream is used and reported. - GUID-defined sections: CRC32 (FC1BCDB0-...) is unwrapped; LZMA (EE4E5898-...) is decoded with the stdlib lzma module; Tiano (A31280AD-...) with the deco

vzdump-verify-prune.sh - Proxmox VE vzdump hook script. Retention rule: keep exactly ONE backup per guest on the backup storage. The previous backup of a guest is deleted only after the new backup of that guest has been written AND verified. Built-in vzdump pruning is expected to be disabled (prune-backups keep-all=1). Install (on the PVE host): install -m 0755 vzdump-verify-prune.sh /usr/local/bin/vzdump-verify-prune.sh then set the backup job's "script" option to /usr/local/bin/vzdump-verify-prune.sh (only for the job(s) that write to the target storage). Hook interface (PVE 8, PVE/VZDump.pm): <script> <phase> [<mode> <vmid>] Environment used: STOREID, DUMPDIR, VMTYPE (qemu|lxc), TARGET (full path of the finished archive). Only phase backup-end acts; all other phases exit 0 silently. backup-end does nothing (exit 0) unless STOREID is set and equals VZDUMP_VERIFY_PRUNE_STOREID; TARGET must be absolute and lie directly in DUMPDIR. Optional environment: DRY_RUN=1 log what would be deleted, delete nothing VZDUMP_VERIFY_PRUNE_LOG log file path (default /var/log/vzdump-verify-prune.log) VZDUMP_VERIFY_PRUNE_STOREID storage this hook manages (default hitachi-data) Exit status: 0 = verified (and pruned), 1 = verification or prune failure (vzdump then marks the guest backup as failed).

Mirror retired Eclipse-infocenter topics from the Internet Archive (Wayback Machine). Built for the Lenovo System x infocenter (https://systemx.lenovofiles.com/help/), whose live host no longer answers. Default target: the System x3650 M3 plugin (machine type 7945, Lenovo and older IBM plugin ids). Commands: mirror Enumerate captures via the CDX API, fetch the newest usable 200 capture of every page (raw, "id_" form, no Wayback toolbar), follow links inside fetched pages to find pages CDX did not list, optionally fetch referenced images, then rebuild text/, MANIFEST.tsv and INDEX.md. Resumable: pages already saved and listed in MANIFEST.tsv are skipped. text Rebuild text/, MANIFEST.tsv titles/hashes and INDEX.md offline from the saved HTML (no network). plugins List plugin ids seen in CDX under the host prefix, optionally filtered by a regular expression (e.g. "imm|7945|4255|7949|7376"). Output layout (default --out sources/infocenter/7945): html/<page>.html raw archived topic HTML as served by Wayback "id_" text/<page>.txt ASCII plain text (headings kept, tables as pipe rows) images/<file> images referenced by the pages (unless --no-images) MANIFEST.tsv page, original URL, snapshot timestamp, sha256, title IMAGES.tsv file, original URL, snapshot timestamp, sha256 FAILED.tsv pages that could not be retrieved, with the reason CDX.

How the public library is generated from the private repository and what the publication filter removes. This library is generated by scripts/build_library.py from the private x3650m3-kb repository and rebuilt on every change. The repository holds the full engineering record; this public edition is filtered by scripts/library_sanitize.py with the rules in site/publish.json.

Identifiers of the owner's unit and lab are replaced by placeholders such as [lab-ip], [mac] or [redacted-id]. Redacted classes: host path, credential file, lab domain, lab ip ten, lab ip guest, mac address, mac ibm compact, proxmox guest, remote access service, lab hostname, and 15 unit identifiers (serial numbers, UUIDs, WWNs and similar). Vendor-documented default addresses and firmware version strings are kept.

Paragraphs, list items and table rows about credentials and key material embedded in vendor firmware images, and about the security posture of the owner's server, are removed completely (10 removal rules). References to security review findings read (security finding, not published). The project state, access map, agent rules and the security review are not published. Firmware binaries and captured server output are listed by name only.
After every build each output file is scanned for every redaction and removal pattern plus an explicit forbidden list; a single finding fails the build and nothing is published.

Facts in the volumes carry a truth level, shown as a coloured badge: MEASUREDCaptured from the owner's own server (command output under captures/).DOCUMENTEDStated in a vendor document (IBM / Lenovo guide, README, changelog).EXTRACTEDRead out of a vendor firmware binary or package.VALIDATEDChecked against a second source or by a test.CANDIDATEInference with a stated reason; not confirmed.INFERREDDerived from other facts; not confirmed.UNKNOWNNot known; no source found yet.NOT VERIFIEDClaimed but not verified.PLANNEDPlanned, not done.
